data.description:
# Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Stage:** intake (draft)

## Problem statement

When the llm-proxy rejects requests with "all providers exhausted",
"all providers unavailable", or "no provider is available during the current
scheduled time window" (HTTP 503), the in-pane recovery loop classifies the
error as a retryable `SERVER_ERROR` and waits out the server-requested
`Retry-After`. While a pane sits in that backoff it holds **no** proxy slot,
so the proxy reports idle and the herdr mode-switch worker flips the shared
proxy to **cheap** on the operator idle window. Cheap mode has *more* slots
than fast (3 vs 1 — `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), so it adds concurrency, and cheap
windows are observed to correlate with exhaustion bursts. Nothing durably
records that a work item is waiting *because the model was unavailable*, so
neither the cheap-switch decision nor the dispatcher can see the difference
between "quiet" and "blocked on a throttled provider".

## Users

- **Operator/producer** running unattended (downtime) dispatch overnight, who
  wants queued work to resume as soon as a model returns, without piling new
  concurrent requests onto an already-exhausted provider pool.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher**, which must know when a waiting job is
  eligible to resume and must not spawn more work while the pool is throttled.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when cloud providers are exhausted, I want the proxy to stay
  in fast mode (or at least not add concurrency) so that my queued jobs do not
  exhaust the pool further.
- As the downtime dispatcher, when a model cooldown elapses, I want to resume
  exactly one waiting pane with a `continue` message rather than opening a
  brand-new pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Durable cooldown record.** When a pane's recovery loop
      classifies a model-unavailable error (`SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion
      patterns) and starts a backoff, a durable, machine-readable record is
      written carrying item id, kind, reason, and `cooldownUntil`; it is
      cleared on the next successful provider response. Verified by unit tests
      of the writer/reader and a write→read→clear round-trip test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cheap-switch gate.** While at least one active model-cooldown
      exists (`cooldownUntil` in the future), the downtime leader's
      `mode-switch-worker.tick()` does **not** POST `cheap`; the hold is
      bounded by `cooldownUntil` (no latch) and the fast-on-command path is
      unaffected. Verified by mode-switch-worker unit tests (cooldown present
      / expired / absent / unreadable).
- [ ] **AC3 — Bounded wake.** At/after `cooldownUntil`, the dispatcher resumes
      **at most one** model-cooldown job via the existing stalled-resume path
      (literal `continue` to a live pane, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an
      exited pane), reusing the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview`
      exclusions. Verified by dispatcher/stalled-work tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Cross-root gate.** A cooldown recorded in any worklog root
      suppresses the machine-wide (shared-proxy) cheap switch. Verified by an
      integration test spanning two roots.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fail-closed and bounded default.** An unreadable/absent signal
      never causes a premature cheap switch (existing fail-closed contract
      preserved); an absent/unparseable `Retry-After` yields a **bounded**
      default cooldown rather than an unbounded hold. Verified by tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover detection, gating, wake,
      cross-root, and failure paths; a regression test proves the previous
      client-side drain is **not** reintroduced (no slot-count completion
      gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded latch).
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
      `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
      changes.

## Constraints

- **Must not reintroduce the withdrawn client drain** (`WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR`):
  no client-side slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded
  latch. The proxy's own server-side bounded drain is unchanged and stays
  authoritative.
- The cheap-switch gate is **bounded by `cooldownUntil`**; it must never block
  the fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`).
- Live pool sizing is fast = 1 slot, cheap = 3 slots
  (`WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), i.e. cheap *increases* concurrency; the gate's only
  purpose is to avoid adding concurrency during known provider exhaustion.
- The mode-switch worker is leader-only and machine-wide, so the cooldown
  signal must be machine-wide for cross-root correctness.
- First increment must not require a new proxy endpoint; a proxy
  provider-availability endpoint is a **follow-up**, not in scope.
- The recovery loop lives in the TUI extension and the consumer in the herdr
  package, so the on-disk signal format is a cross-package contract and must
  be versioned/tolerant (unknown fields ignored).

## Existing state

- **Detection exists, but is ephemeral.** `error-patterns.ts` classifies the
  exhaustion bodies as `SERVER_ERROR`; `resolveRetryDelay()` /
  `parseRetryAfterHeaders()` (`retry-logic.ts`) extract the server-requested
  delay (ceiling 6 h) and `register-recovery.ts:406` computes it. The result
  lives only in in-memory `RetryState`.
- **No durable model-cooldown state.** The rolling
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (`downtime-log.ts`) has dispatch markers
  and pane-close `reasonCode`s but no cooldown entry; the worklog
  `needsProducerReview` flag is unrelated.
- **Wake machinery already exists.** `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` (`stalled-work.ts`) prompt a live pane with the literal
  `continue`, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an exited pane, and the
  dispatcher already prefers resuming a stalled pane over opening a new one
  (`WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1`). Its trigger is "not working ≥ threshold", gated by
  the non-terminal cooldown and attempt cap — with **no model-availability
  input**.
- **The cheap path is blind.** `mode-switch-worker.tick()` switches to cheap on
  `operator idle ≥ threshold AND evaluateIdle(proxyStatus)`; a pane in backoff
  holds zero slots, so this looks idle.
- **The proxy cannot report exhaustion today.** `LlamaStatus`
  (`/llama/local/status`) exposes local server/slot/lease state only; there is
  no provider-availability field.

## Desired change

1. **Emit/clear a durable cooldown marker.** On `SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion in
   `register-recovery.ts`, write a record with `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs`
   (item id, kind, reason), machine-wide so any root can read it; clear it when
   `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` observes the next 2xx.
2. **Gate the cheap switch.** Read the marker in the leader's `tick()` (same
   pattern as `readSharedActivity`); while any cooldown is active, hold fast.
3. **Wake one job at expiry.** Feed expired cooldown candidates into the
   existing stalled-resume path so exactly one pane is resumed.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` — the versioned cooldown contract and
  tolerant reader/writer shared by both packages (new).
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts` — contract tests (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — coordination-dir resolver
  (delegates to the shared resolver; single source of truth).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — writes
  the cooldown marker on `SERVER_ERROR`, clears it on the next 2xx.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — exposes the
  resolved cooldown (`cooldownUntil`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — bounded
  default cooldown in the recovery configuration.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — reads the cooldown signal and
  gates the cheap switch.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — gate unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts` — expired-cooldown candidate source.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatcher branch that resumes one
  cooldown candidate at expiry.
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` — behaviour and contract documentation.

**Corrections from the predicted list (plan time):**
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` is **dropped** — the signal is
machine-wide, not the per-root dispatch log (decision Q2 = A). The bounded
default lives in the recovery configuration in the TUI extension (which owns
the cooldown computation), not in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`; herdr only
reads the resulting signal.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R: Waking before providers return just re-fails** and burns the per-item
  attempt budget until `needsProducerReview` trips. **Mitigation:** gate the
  wake strictly on `cooldownUntil`; prefer a proxy provider-availability
  signal when one exists (follow-up).
- **R: The premise is unproven.** Cheap mode may help (local-first) or hurt
  (more concurrency) depending on why providers are exhausted.
  **Mitigation:** RESOLVED BY DECISION — the producer accepted the premise
  (interview round 2, Q1 = B): the cooldown machinery is built without a Phase 0
  log-mining gate, so this risk remains open and accepted, not mitigated.
- **R: `Retry-After` may be absent**, making the cooldown best-effort.
  **Mitigation:** bounded default cooldown setting; document best-effort.
- **R: Cross-root staleness** — a crashed pane leaves a stale marker.
  **Mitigation:** `cooldownUntil` TTL + clear-on-success + fail-closed reads.
- **R: Scope creep** into proxy (cross-repo) changes. **Mitigation:** record
  proxy endpoint work as a linked follow-up, not in this item.
- **A1 (VERIFIED at plan time):** the recovery loop can extract the item
  id/kind from `ctx` session entries best-effort. Verified: the TUI extension
  has no herdr import and no pane-label access, so the marker is keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId` (plus a best-effort `itemId`) and the dispatcher resolves
  item and kind from the pane label it already reads for the stalled scan. See
  "Plan-time verification".
- **A2 (CONFIRMED by decision Q2 = A):** a machine-wide JSON file in the
  coordination directory (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`)
  is the transport for the first increment, implemented as a versioned shared
  contract (`@worklog/shared/model-cooldown`).

## Decisions (interview round 2 — resolved)

Producer answers recorded 2026-10-12 in the plan session (session id in the
work-item comments):

1. **Build now vs investigate first → BUILD NOW (option B).** The cooldown
   machinery is built without a Phase 0 log-mining gate; the operator accepts
   that "cheap windows worsen exhaustion" is not yet proven. Consequence: no
   investigation gate in the plan; the premise risk stays open and is recorded
   in the appendix. There is therefore **no Phase 0 gate child**.
2. **Cooldown signal source → CLIENT RECOVERY-LOOP MARKER (option A).** The TUI
   recovery loop writes and clears a versioned, machine-wide JSON marker in the
   machine coordination directory (`HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` or
   `~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`), best-effort from
   `Retry-After`. A proxy provider-availability endpoint is a separate
   follow-up, not in scope.
3. **Wake trigger → STRICTLY AT/AFTER `cooldownUntil`, ONE JOB PER CYCLE
   (option A).** The wake reuses the existing stalled-resume path and its
   safety gates (attempt cap, `needsProducerReview`); no early wake and no
   batch wake.

**Plan-time verification of assumption A1:** the TUI recovery loop has no
herdr import and no pane-label access, so it cannot derive `itemId`/`kind`
from the pane label. The marker therefore carries `cooldownUntil`, `reason`,
`paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and `sessionId`, with `itemId` derived best-effort
from session entries (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`); the herdr dispatcher
resolves `itemId` + `kind` from the pane label it already reads for the stalled
scan (`paneLabelItemId`, `downtime-worker.ts`). The record format is versioned
JSON with unknown fields ignored.


## Plan (features)

Decomposed 2026-10-12 into 7 vertical-slice child items, created test-first
(the contract slice first, then the behaviour slices, then documentation and
verification). No Phase 0 investigation gate (decision Q1 = B).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|------------|------------|
| 1 | `WL-0MV563825002R9Y1` Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader | task | — | AC1, AC6 |
| 2 | `WL-0MV5638J1006URXA` Recovery loop records durable cooldown | feature | 1 | AC1 |
| 3 | `WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ` Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns | feature | 1 | AC2, AC4 |
| 4 | `WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7` Bounded wake of one cooled-down job | feature | 1 | AC3 |
| 5 | `WL-0MV5639X70029BOI` Bounded default cooldown and fail-closed hardening | feature | 2 | AC5 |
| 6 | `WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H` Cooldown behaviour documentation | docs | 2,3,4,5 | AC7 |
| 7 | `WL-0MV563AU2007FM56` Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification | task | 2,3,4,5 | AC6, AC8 |

Test-first ordering: child 1 (the contract/verification slice) is created first
and blocks every behaviour child; children 2–5 each write their tests before
their implementation; children 6–7 verify and document the finished behaviour.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-12T11:13Z — interview round 2 asked (3 multiple-choice questions, each
  with an explicit agent recommendation); questions recorded verbatim as a
  work-item comment.
- 2026-10-12T11:14Z — producer answered B / A / A; questions resolved in the
  appendix above.
- 2026-10-12T11:29Z — feature breakdown produced and reviewed; 7 children
  created in test-first order with dependency edges; AC coverage verified at
  100% (`proceed`).
- 2026-10-12T11:31Z — effort/risk recomputed against the 7-child WBS:
  effort Large (expected 65 h, recommended 89 h, range 54–144 h), risk High
  (score 14), confidence 88%; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9` — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching
  (the behaviour this builds on).
- `WL-0MUL0KO7Q003O7YJ` — Drain before switching to cheap (withdrawn).
- `WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR` — Revert drain-before-cheap (must not regress to this).
- `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM` — Drain-before-cheap threshold unsatisfiable in fast
  mode (1-slot pool); live pool sizing.
- `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` — Honour long server `Retry-After` hints.
- `WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1` — Scan for stalled work before dispatching.
- `WL-0MUYMBPZ5004LBFX` — In-place resume orchestrator.
- `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` — Classify "All providers unavailable … time window"
  503 as `SERVER_ERROR`.
- `WL-0MUY9GDPG0062NWF` — Cap recovery retry-loop backoff at 10 m.
- `WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5` — Minimum cooldown before re-dispatching after a
  non-terminal pane close.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 2 was asked interactively in the plan session (session id recorded in the
work-item comments); answers received 2026-10-12.

- **Q1:** Should we implement immediately, or investigate the fast/cheap ×
  exhaustion correlation first? — **Answer (producer, in-session): option B —
  build now; the unproven premise is accepted.** Options offered: (A) Phase 0
  evidence check first (agent recommendation); (B) build now; (C) drop the
  item. **Final: B.** Consequence: no investigation gate; the prerequisite
  risk stays open (see "Open questions carried forward").
- **Q2:** What is the source of the model-cooldown signal? — **Answer

  machine-wide coordination dir.** Options: (A) client marker, `Retry-After`
  best-effort, proxy endpoint as a follow-up (agent recommendation); (B) wait
  for a proxy provider-availability endpoint; (C) per-worklog file. **Final:
  A.** Evidence: repo analysis — `LlamaStatus` has no provider field; AC4
  requires cross-root reach; the constraint forbids a new proxy endpoint in
  increment 1.
- **Q3:** What triggers the wake? — **Answer (producer, in-session): option A —
  strictly at/after `cooldownUntil`, at most one job per cycle, reusing the
  stalled-resume safety gates.** Options: (A) strict/one-at-a-time (agent
  recommendation); (B) also wake early on a proxy probe; (C) wake all cooled
  down jobs at once. **Final: A.** Evidence: AC3; `resumeStalledPane` /
  `classifyStalledPane` attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview` exclusions.

**Resolved at plan time (no producer decision needed):** assumption A1 — the

# Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Lock the cross-package, versioned on-disk contract for the model-cooldown
marker **before** any behaviour slice, so the TUI writer and the herdr reader
cannot drift (parent constraint: the on-disk signal format is a cross-package
contract and must be versioned/tolerant, with unknown fields ignored).

## Target outcome

One shared module (the same pattern as the existing
`@worklog/shared/lease-release`) provides the contract and the tolerant
reader/writer used by both packages:

- `resolveMachineCoordinationDir()` — `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override (with
  `~` expansion) else `~/.herdr/downtime`; `null` when unresolvable.
- `readModelCooldowns(dir, now)` — active entries only (`cooldownUntil` in the
  future); tolerant (unknown fields ignored, malformed entries skipped); `[]`
  for a missing file; fails closed when the file is unreadable/corrupt.
- `writeModelCooldown(dir, entry)` — atomic (temp file + rename) upsert keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId`, pruning expired entries.
- `clearModelCooldown(dir, key)` — remove one entry; a missing file is a no-op.

Record shape (versioned; unknown fields ignored by readers):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "cooldowns": [
    {
      "paneId": "<herdr pane id>",
      "sessionId": "<pi session id>",
      "itemId": "WL-... or null",
      "kind": "plan|intake|implement|audit|risk-effort or null",
      "reason": "all providers exhausted",
      "createdAt": 1700000000000,
      "cooldownUntil": 1700000300000
    }
  ]
}
```

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first for the five behaviours below (round trip, tolerance, malformed
   entry, expiry prune, missing vs unreadable, dir resolution).
2. The shared module implementing the functions and owning the field semantics
   (its header comment is the contract of record).
3. Export the subpath from the shared package manifest.
4. Make the herdr `getMachineCoordinationDir()` delegate to the shared resolver
   so there is a single source of truth (its existing tests must stay green).
5. No behaviour change in the herdr or TUI packages in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A durable, versioned, machine-readable cooldown contract exists with `schemaVersion` and tolerant readers (unknown fields ignored) in the shared package, importable by both the TUI recovery loop and herdr.
- [ ] A write-read-clear round-trip test proves a record with cooldownUntil and its pane/session key is written, read back and cleared.
- [ ] Tolerant reads: malformed entries are skipped and unknown fields are ignored without throwing, verified by tests.
- [ ] Expiry: entries with cooldownUntil in the past are not active and are pruned on the next write, verified by tests.
- [ ] Fail-closed reads: a missing or corrupt file is distinguished, verified by tests.
- [ ] Memory: the herdr coordination-dir resolver delegates to the shared one and its existing tests pass.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (the AC extraction used by planning tooling reads only
the first line of each bullet, so the full wording lives here).

- AC1 elaborates parent AC1 ("Durable cooldown record"): the record is durable
  (on disk, machine-wide) and machine-readable; it carries `paneId`/`sessionId`
  as the key plus `itemId`, `kind`, `reason`, `createdAt`, `cooldownUntil`.
- AC2: writer then reader then clearer, asserting the entry disappears.
- AC3: `{"schemaVersion": 1, "cooldowns": [{"paneId": "p"}]}` (missing fields)
  and `{"cooldowns": "not-an-array"}` must not throw.
- AC4: a past `cooldownUntil` is filtered out of `readModelCooldowns` and
  removed by the next `writeModelCooldown`.
- AC5: `null`/absent dir, a non-JSON file, and an unreadable file each resolve
  deterministically.
- AC6: `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`, `~/`-prefixed values, and the `~/.herdr/downtime`
  default are asserted through the shared resolver.

## Deliverables

- The shared cooldown-contract module and its unit tests.
- The subpath export in the shared package manifest.
- The herdr coordination-dir resolver delegating to the shared resolver, with
  its existing tests still green.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/package.json`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Created first: the contract/verification slice (test-first ordering) and a
prerequisite for every behaviour slice below.

# Recovery loop records durable cooldown

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

When the in-pane recovery loop classifies a model-unavailable error as
`SERVER_ERROR` (exhaustion patterns: "all providers exhausted", "all providers
unavailable", "no provider is available during the current scheduled time
window") and starts a backoff, write a durable machine-wide cooldown marker;
clear it on the next successful provider response. Today that state lives only
in in-memory `RetryState`.

## Target outcome

- Exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` → write a marker with
  `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs` via the shared contract from the contract
  slice.
- The next 2xx observed by `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` → clear the marker.
- `itemId`/`kind` derived best-effort from `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`
  (first user message carrying a work-item id and a dispatch-kind token); left
  `null` when not derivable — the dispatcher then resolves them from the pane
  label. The marker key is always `paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) + `sessionId`.
- Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts
  the retry loop.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first: write on exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` using the resolved delay; no
   write for a non-exhaustion retryable error; clear on 2xx; id/kind derivation
   present and absent; missing `HERDR_PANE_ID` degrades to a session-only key;
   an unwritable directory does not throw.
2. Expose `cooldownUntil` (`now + delayMs`) from `resolveRetryDelay()` without
   changing the existing `delayMs`/`serverHintMs` results.
3. Call the writer from the `SERVER_ERROR` branch of `register-recovery.ts` and
   the clearer from the existing 2xx path of `installFetchRetryHintCapture()`.
4. Keep the notify/stale-ctx safety contract intact (no new throwing paths).
5. Update the source comments describing the retry loop's side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Durable cooldown record: when a pane's recovery loop starts a backoff, a durable record with cooldownUntil is written and cleared on success.
- [ ] Detection: an exhaustion SERVER_ERROR writes the marker and a plain retryable 5xx or timeout does not, verified by tests.
- [ ] Item identity: itemId and kind are derived from session entries when present and left null when absent, with the pane/session key always written.
- [ ] Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts the retry loop, verified by tests.
- [ ] Constraint: no slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause and no unbounded latch are introduced.

bullet).

# Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

The herdr mode-switch worker must not switch the machine-wide proxy to `cheap`
while any active model-cooldown exists. A pane sitting in proxy backoff holds no
slot, so the proxy looks idle and the leader currently flips the shared proxy to
cheap — adding concurrency (cheap has more slots than fast) during a known
provider-exhaustion window.

## Target outcome

- `mode-switch-worker.tick()` reads the shared cooldown signal (the same
  pattern as `readSharedActivity`) and holds **fast** while any `cooldownUntil`
  is in the future.
- The hold is bounded by `cooldownUntil`: no latch, no persisted state — the
  first tick after expiry performs the normal idle/cheap decision.
- The fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`) is unaffected.
- Reach is machine-wide: a cooldown written for any worklog root suppresses the
  shared-proxy cheap switch (the coordination dir is machine-wide, not per-root).

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the mode-switch worker test file: cooldown present → no cheap
   POST; expired → cheap POST; absent → cheap POST; unreadable/corrupt →
   fail-closed (no cheap POST); fast path still POSTs `fast` while a cooldown is
   active.
2. Read the cooldown signal in `tick()` before the mode read and return early
   when any entry is active; keep the coordination dir injectable for tests.
3. Cross-root integration test: a marker written for one root suppresses the
   switch when the worker is configured for another root (one machine-wide
   coordination dir, two roots).
4. Update the mode-switch design doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC2 — Cheap-switch gate: while at least one active model-cooldown exists, tick does not POST cheap; the hold is bounded by cooldownUntil.
- [ ] AC4 — Cross-root gate: a cooldown recorded in any worklog root suppresses the cheap switch.
- [ ] Fast path: onOperatorCommand still POSTs fast while a cooldown is active, verified by a test.
- [ ] No latch: the first tick at or after cooldownUntil performs the normal cheap decision, verified by a test.
- [ ] Fail-closed: an unreadable or corrupt signal produces no cheap POST, verified by a test.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC2 (parent AC2 "Cheap-switch gate"): the four-unit-test matrix is cooldown
  present / expired / absent / unreadable, each asserting the cheap POST or its
  absence, plus an assertion that the fast-on-command path is untouched.
- AC4 (parent AC4 "Cross-root gate"): write the marker through the shared store
  for root A, construct the worker for root B, assert no cheap POST; this is the
  integration test spanning two roots.
- No latch: after expiry the tick performs `GET /admin/mode` and the normal
  switch decision exactly as before the change.
- Fail-closed direction: "no cheap switch" is the safe direction (the proxy
  stays fast); the condition is logged so it is not silent.
- The withdrawn client drain must not return: no slot-count completion gate, no
  dispatch pause, no unbounded latch in the gate path.

## Deliverables

- The mode-switch gate change plus its unit tests.
- The cross-root integration test.
- The updated mode-switch design document.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts`

# Bounded wake of one cooled-down job

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

At or after `cooldownUntil`, resume **at most one** model-cooldown job through
the existing stalled-resume path (literal `continue` to a live pane, or a
relaunch of pi `--continue` in an exited pane) rather than waiting for the
generic stall threshold or opening a brand-new pane.

## Target outcome

- The dispatcher consults the shared cooldown signal and, when at least one
  entry has expired, feeds that candidate into the existing stalled-resume
  machinery — at most one resume per cycle.
- The existing safety gates still apply: the non-terminal pane-close cooldown,
  the per-item/per-kind attempt cap, and the `needsProducerReview` exclusion.
- A successful resume consumes/clears the marker so the same pane is not woken
  repeatedly; a failed resume stays bounded by `cooldownUntil` and the attempt
  cap.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the stalled-work and downtime-worker dispatch test files:
   expired cooldown yields a candidate; unexpired cooldown does not; at most one
   resume per cycle; the attempt cap and `needsProducerReview` still exclude a
   cooldown candidate; a successful resume consumes the marker.
2. Add an expired-cooldown candidate source in `stalled-work.ts` (mapping
   `paneId` to the pane record the scan already reads) or extend
   `classifyStalledPane` with the cooldown input.
3. Wire it into the dispatcher's pre-dispatch stalled scan seam so at most one
   cooldown resume happens per cycle, preferring it over opening a new pane.
4. Ensure the wake uses the unchanged `STALLED_RESUME_PROMPT` and the existing
   attempt accounting.
5. Update the downtime-dispatcher doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC3 — Bounded wake: at/after cooldownUntil the dispatcher resumes at most one job via the stalled-resume path.
- [ ] Strictness: an unexpired cooldown never wakes a pane, verified by tests.
- [ ] Safety gates: a cooldown candidate is still excluded by the attempt cap and by the needsProducerReview flag, verified by tests.
- [ ] Bounded concurrency: at most one cooldown resume per dispatcher cycle, verified by tests.
- [ ] Consumption: a successful resume consumes the marker so it is not re-woken on the next cycle; a failed resume remains bounded, verified by tests.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC3 (parent AC3 "Bounded wake"): reuse `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` — the literal `continue` prompt to a live pane and the pi
  `--continue` relaunch for an exited pane both stay the only wake mechanisms;
  the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview` exclusions are asserted against a
  cooldown-sourced candidate.
- Strictness: `cooldownUntil` in the future must not produce a wake even when
  the generic stall threshold has elapsed.
- Bounded concurrency: the cycle reports `{ ok: true, stalledResume: true }` on
  one resume and must not offer new work in the same cycle.
- Failed resume: a neutral failure reason is not turned into a CLI-error strike,
  a crash or a duplicate resume.

## Deliverables

- The expired-cooldown candidate source and the dispatcher wiring.
- The stalled-work and dispatcher test coverage.
- The updated downtime-dispatcher developer document.

# Bounded default cooldown and fail-closed hardening

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Make the cooldown best-effort but never unbounded, and keep every failure path
fail-closed: an absent or unparseable `Retry-After` yields a bounded default
cooldown, and an unreadable signal never causes a premature cheap switch.

## Target outcome

- A bounded default cooldown (with a documented clamp floor and ceiling) is used
  when the recovery loop has no usable server hint.
- An absent or malformed `Retry-After` yields that bounded default — never an
  unbounded hold and never a zero hold.
- A truthful long hint stays clamped by the existing server-hint ceiling
  (6 hours), so no unbounded hold is possible.
- The gate distinguishes an absent/empty signal (normal cheap decision) from an
  unreadable/corrupt signal (hold fast, log the condition).
- Stale markers left by a crashed pane expire by `cooldownUntil` and are pruned
  on write.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the recovery settings and retry-logic test files: no hint →
   bounded default; malformed hint → bounded default; an over-ceiling honest
   hint is clamped.
2. Add the bounded default (and its clamp) to the recovery config defaults in
   `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG`, documented alongside the existing
   `baseDelayMs`/`maxDelayMs` per-category values.
3. Sharpen the shared reader so absent, empty, unreadable and corrupt are
   distinguishable by callers.
4. Mode-switch gate tests: unreadable/corrupt → no cheap POST and a log; absent
   → the normal cheap decision.
5. Settings/pruning tests: a stale marker expires and is pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC5 — Fail-closed and bounded default: an unreadable/absent signal never switches cheap early; an absent Retry-After yields a bounded default cooldown.
- [ ] Bounded default: a documented default with a clamp floor and ceiling exists in the recovery configuration, verified by settings tests.
- [ ] Clamped ceiling: an honest server hint above the ceiling is clamped rather than honoured unbounded, verified by tests.
- [ ] Absent vs unreadable: an absent/empty signal permits the normal cheap decision while an unreadable/corrupt signal holds fast and is logged, verified by tests.
- [ ] Staleness: a marker from a crashed pane expires by cooldownUntil and is pruned on the next write, verified by tests.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC5 (parent AC5 "Fail-closed and bounded default"): "fail-closed" here means
  the proxy stays fast (no cheap POST) — never a premature cheap switch; the
  bounded default prevents an unbounded hold when the server gives no hint.
- Bounded default home: the retry loop (which owns the cooldown computation)
  lives in the TUI extension, so the default belongs in the recovery
  configuration rather than the herdr settings schema; the herdr side only
  reads the resulting signal.
- Clamped ceiling: reuse the existing `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (6 h) so a
  truthful long `Retry-After` keeps working (WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) while a
  malformed or absurd value cannot pin the cooldown open.
- Staleness: the writer prunes expired entries; the reader never reports an
  expired entry as active.

## Deliverables

- The bounded default cooldown (with clamp) in the recovery configuration.
- The clamped-ceiling and absent-vs-unreadable behaviour and their tests.
- The stale-marker expiry/prune tests.
- The updated README settings documentation.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/settings.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/README.md`

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`.

This caused the finish to crash after committing and removing the worktree, leaving the implementation lost and the work item reset to `open`.

Implement `watchDbChanges` in `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Goal
A cheap, cross-process-safe watch over the worklog change signal so the pane can react to an agent write promptly.

## Scope
- `watchDbChanges(cacheDir, worklogDir, opts)`: watches the state-counter file (`state/<hash>.json`) and/or `worklog.db`/`-wal`, debounces/coalesces bursts, and emits a change callback.
- Fail open: any watch/read error is reported as unavailable so the caller falls back to polling. Never throws into the TUI loop.
- `dispose()`/`close()` for teardown on pane exit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `watchDbChanges` watches the cross-process DB-change signal (state counter and/or SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal`), debounces events, and emits at most one change callback per burst.
- The watch fails open: any read or `fs.watch` error is reported as unavailable and the caller falls back to the 30 s auto-refresh tick.
- Watch teardown (`dispose`) removes all `fs.watch` handles and timers.
- Unit tests cover the watch trigger, debounce/coalescing, and fail-open fallback, with injected `fs.watch`/clock.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer `node:fs` `watch` (no new runtime dependencies). Handle the state-counter file being absent at start-up (watch the `state/` directory or fall back to polling).
- Inject `fs.watch`/timers for deterministic tests (mirror the `db-change.test.ts` mocking style).

## Dependencies
- F1 verification harness (shared contract tests).

# implement.py finish crashes in the non-fast-forward rebase-retry path

**Discovered from:** WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ

## Problem

When `implement.py finish` commits successfully but `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`
is rejected as non-fast-forward (dev advanced concurrently), the recovery
path raises an unhandled exception:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

## Location

Global implement skill (not tracked in this repo):
`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`, in the
`PushNonFastForwardError` handler (~line 4305):

```python
rebase_result = run_cmd(
    ["git", "rebase", "origin/dev"],
    cwd=cwd,          # <-- NameError: 'cwd' is not defined in this scope
)
```

The surrounding function has `repo_root`, `branch`, `worktree_path` — no `cwd`.

## Impact

- The finish phase has ALREADY committed and removed the worktree by this point,
  so the agent is left with: work committed on the local feature branch, the
  worktree deleted, status reset to `open`, and nothing pushed.
- Requires manual recovery (fetch, re-create worktree for the branch, rebase onto
  `origin/dev`, push).
- Secondary issue: the retry pushes from `repo_root` (main checkout) and the
  rebase (if it ran) would target the checked-out branch, not the feature
  branch — the rebase should run against the feature branch before worktree
  removal, or use an explicit ref.

## Reproduction

1. Start an implementation; let it commit.
2. Push `dev` from another actor between the worktree fork and the finish push
   so the finish push is rejected non-fast-forward.
3. `implement.py finish` raises `name 'cwd' is not defined` after committing and
   removing the worktree.

## Observed in

WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ (cheap-switch gate): finish committed `180b9775`, removed the
worktree, then crashed; recovered by rebasing the branch onto `origin/dev` and
pushing (`a6f5ca98`).

In a multi-agent repo, another agent's implement.py finish fast-forwards the main checkout's refs/heads/dev and creates/removes its own agent worktree; the guard attributes these to the tested suite and sets success=False (live_repo_mutation), blocking implement.py finish and test verification even though every test passed.

Discovered during WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6 (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6).

## Problem
`implement.py finish`'s test gate failed twice with a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict even though the canonical suite passed (both declared commands exited 0). The guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, used by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) snapshots refs, local `.git/config`, registered worktrees, and `git status` before/after the suite. On a multi-agent host with several active worktrees, concurrent agent activity moved:
- `refs/remotes/origin/dev` (observed bbc8e89a -> 4163175)
- `refs/heads/dev` (main checkout's local dev, advanced by another agent's finish fast-forward)
- another agent's feature branch ref

Only refs checked out in agent worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` (and their `branch.<name>.*` config) are excluded, so these deltas fail the gate.

## Impact
`implement.py finish` fails after a ~17-minute suite run and resets the item to `open`; the agent must sync its worktree to the latest `dev` and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Possible fix
Exclude `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*` (or ignore ref movement entirely) from the mutation diff while still catching working-tree mutations caused by the suite itself; or scope the ref check to refs the suite could plausibly touch.

## Workaround
Fast-forward the worktree to the latest `origin/dev`, run the full suite once to warm the per-command cache, then re-run `implement.py finish` (cache hits shrink the race window).

# Intake Brief: Migrate downtime-worker tests from toHaveBeenCalledWith to observable-outcome assertions

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** AC4 required assertions to prefer observable
outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators
(`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). The 13-child split preserved all
existing assertions verbatim — **137** `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences
before and after — and AC4 was deferred to this follow-up. The assertions are
therefore unreviewed: some legitimately assert the unit's observable contract
(calls to injected dependencies and boundary adapters), while others couple
tests to implementation detail (child-process event wiring) or duplicate a
behaviour already asserted through the returned outcome.

## Users

- **Maintainer / AI agent** — needs downtime-worker tests that survive
  refactoring because they assert the unit's observable contract rather than
  its internal wiring.
- **Reviewer** — needs an auditable classification showing every retained
  assertion is intentional and every migration preserves behavioural coverage.

## Evidence and baseline

Baseline across `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (commit
`b195e01a`):

| File | `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences |
|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` | 37 |
| `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` | 22 |
| `downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` | 21 |
| `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` | 15 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` | 14 |
| `downtime-worker.test.ts` | 13 |
| `downtime-worker.sprint-view.test.ts` | 8 |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` | 3 |
| `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` | 2 |
| `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` | 2 |
| **Total** | **137** |

(Includes 18 `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` and 8 negative
`.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` forms; 4 occurrences are `handle.once` child-process
event-wiring shape assertions.)

Targets are mock collaborators only — the files contain **zero** `vi.mock()`
calls. The overwhelming majority of occurrences target injected `deps.*`
functions (`spawnAgentPane` 34, `claimItem` 17, `rollbackClaim` 4,
`recordDispatch`/`recordDispatchFailure` 7, tier lookups, etc.) or test-local
mock adapters injected as dependencies. A small minority target non-boundary
internals (`handle.once`) or observable output streams (`stderrSpy`) or
injected adapters (`spawnFn`, `fetcher`, `callback`).

## Scope decision (producer, Q1-A)

The producer approved this classification rule:

- **Boundary / observable contract → retain (justified).** A call on an
  injected `deps` function or an injected boundary adapter
  (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`, `closePane`, `spawnFn`, `fetcher`,
  `callback`, anchors, reapers, `dep`, …) is the unit's observable contract
  because the entry points take `deps` as an argument; there is no other
  observable channel for these side effects. Observable output streams
  (`stderrSpy`) are likewise observable outcomes.
- **Internal / redundant → migrate.** (a) Implementation-detail wiring such as
  `handle.once('error'|'exit', …)` shape assertions where the same test already
  drives the listener and asserts the resulting `spawned` outcome; (b)
  redundant call-shape/query assertions whose behaviour is already proven by a
  returned outcome/state (e.g. a tier query when `outcome.kind` and
  `outcome.candidate` are asserted).
- **Ordering assertions** (`toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` proving tier/fallback
  order) are retained unless an outcome assertion proves the identical
  ordering; otherwise they carry unique behavioural coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Classification complete.** Every `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrence in
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (baseline 137) is recorded in
   a classification table posted as a work-item comment — file, line, category
   (`retain` / `migrate`), and a one-line reason — and the category counts
   reconcile to the baseline total.
2. **Internal/redundant assertions migrated.** Every occurrence classified
   `migrate` is converted so the same behaviour is asserted through an
   observable outcome (returned value/state), or removed only where an
   existing assertion in the same test already proves that behaviour.
   Verification: `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith'
   packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts` returns zero matches.
3. **Retained assertions justified.** Every retained occurrence carries a short
   inline comment stating why the dependency call is the unit's observable
   contract, and appears in the classification table (producer Q2-A).
4. **Behavioural coverage preserved.** No downtime-worker test case is deleted;
   the test-case count is unchanged; for every removed assertion the
   classification table names the outcome assertion that replaces it. Only
   `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files change (no production-code change).
5. **Parent AC4 satisfied.** An evidence comment is posted on
   WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX linking this item and its outcome; the parent is not
   reopened or re-audited (producer Q3-A).
6. **Documentation and full suite.** All related documentation and code
   comments are updated to reflect the changes; the full project test suite
   passes with the new changes (run via `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Do not change production code — the change is confined to
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (plus inline comments).
- Preserve test semantics; no assertion may be dropped without a named
  replacement or an explicit table justification.
- All written output in UK English.
- Do not introduce new test dependencies.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- 14 `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files (13 split files plus
  `downtime-worker.test.ts`), 137 `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences, zero
  `vi.mock()` calls.
- Shared scaffolding (`makeDeps`, status fixtures, temp-dir helpers) lives in
  `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`.
- Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** is `completed`/`done`; AC4 was deferred to
  this item by producer decision.

## Desired change

Apply the producer-approved classification to every occurrence, migrate the
internal/redundant subset to observable-outcome assertions, annotate the
retained subset, publish the classification table, and close the deferred
parent AC4 with an evidence comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — largest target (37); mostly boundary deps + redundant `getNextItem` queries
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — boundary deps, `stderrSpy`, ordering assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` — boundary deps, negative assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — tier-ordering (`Nth`) assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — `handle.once` wiring (migration target), injected `spawnFn`/`callback`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — `resumeStalledPane` boundary assertion
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.sprint-view.test.ts` — injected `dep`/`getHerdrListHead`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — injected `fetcher`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — small boundary counts
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — source of the anti-pattern guidance (reference only; no change)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-migration weakens regression coverage.** Mitigation: every
  removal must be paired with the outcome assertion that replaces it, named in
  the classification table.
- **Risk: mechanical removal of ordering assertions hides tier-ordering
  regressions.** Mitigation: retain `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` ordering
  assertions unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering.
- **Assumption (producer-approved):** injected `deps`/boundary-adapter calls are
  observable outcomes, not internal collaborators (Q1-A).
- **Risk: scope creep.** Do not migrate `toHaveBeenCalledWith` outside
  `downtime-worker.*.test.ts`; other test suites are out of scope (record as a
  separate work item if desired).
- **Risk: classification ambiguity.** Unresolved cases are retained with an
  explicit justification, never silently dropped.

## Related work

- **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** — Split `downtime-worker.test.ts` and cap mocks per test (parent; AC4 deferred)
- **WL-0MV4VEQOZ005XH34** — Split settings and worker state tests into a dedicated file (split child)
- **WL-0MUNMCZ2K003DZ50** — F2: Wire drain signal to downtime worker dispatch (touches these tests)
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which assertions count as "internal collaborator" and must migrate?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A** — migrate only non-boundary
  internals (`handle.once` event wiring, global `fetch`/`fetcher`,
  `console`/`stderr` spies, poll `callback`) and redundant query-call
  assertions already proven by a returned outcome; injected `deps`/boundary
  assertions are retained with justification. Source: interactive reply,
  session `herdr-1792000712-930434-30101`.
- **Q2 — Where should retained-assertion justifications live?**
  Answer (producer): **A** — inline comment per retained assertion **plus** a
  summary classification table on the work item. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — How is parent AC4 "satisfied" given the parent is already
  `completed`/`done`?** Answer (producer): **A** — post an evidence comment on
  WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX; do not reopen/re-audit the parent. Source: interactive
  reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MUNMCZ2K003DZ50** – F2: Wire drain signal to downtime worker dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MV4VEQOZ005XH34** – Split settings and worker state tests into dedicated file (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: ac4, acceptance, agent, already, ambiguity (+234 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: ac4, agent, already, ambiguity, anchors (+219 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: agent, already, answer, answers, anti (+182 more)

Discovered from: WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (producer-rejection fix).

The default-view refresh path opens a FRESH WorklogDatabase connection per withInProcessDb call — twice per refresh (fetchActionableCount + fetchChildrenForItems). Each open is a synchronous better-sqlite3 operation (~46-70 ms on the 100 MB worklog.db, including initializeSchema/initializeFts DDL) that blocks the TUI event loop. After the WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN loop fix (counter-only watch), refreshes are occasional so this is a transient hiccup, not continuous lag; but it violates the strict reading of the <=100 ms p95 input-lag budget when a refresh coincides with typing.

Proposal: open ONE connection per refresh, share it between the actionable-count and children reads, close in a finally; or move the in-process read off the critical render path. Keep the no-stale-cache invariant (never serve from the store's in-memory query cache across a refresh boundary) by still closing per refresh.
data.title: Herdr: share one in-process SQLite connection per refresh to bound event-loop blocking

# Intake Brief — Don't open pane for recording reviews (WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ)

**Headline**: When a herdr selection-list shortcut declares `open_pane: false` but also contains an unknown placeholder (e.g. `a-r`'s `<reason>`), the placeholder form dialog dispatches the command without forwarding the `open_pane` flag, so a visible command pane still opens. The fix forwards `openPane` (and `onRefresh`/`focus`) through the form-dialog dispatch path so `a-r` — and any future placeholder shortcut with `open_pane: false` — runs in the background.

## Problem statement

In the herdr selection list, pressing `a-r` (audit reject) is configured in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` with `"open_pane": false`, which is supposed to run the command in the background with no pane (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL). However, `a-r`'s command template contains an unknown placeholder (`<reason>`), so it is intercepted by the form dialog (`form-dialog.ts`) to collect the rejection reason. The form dialog's `onSubmit` handler calls `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model ?? undefined)` directly, passing only two arguments and dropping the resolved `openPane` flag. As a result, a visible "Command Output" pane opens even though the shortcut explicitly opted out of a pane. Identical shortcuts without a placeholder (`a-y`, `u-p-*`, `x-c`, `x-d`) correctly run in the background, confirming the form-dialog path is the specific point of failure.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** using `a-r` (audit reject) on `in_review` items in the herdr selection list. They expect a quiet, non-intrusive rejection that just updates the item state.
  - *As a reviewer, I want to reject an item with a reason and have it recorded silently in the background, so I don't have to dismiss a command-output pane after every rejection.*
- **Herdr plugin users generally**: any shortcut entry that combines an unknown placeholder with `open_pane: false` (current and future entries) should honour the no-pane contract.

### User stories

- As a reviewer, when I press `a-r` and enter a rejection reason, the command runs in the background (no pane opens), the item is rejected, and the list refreshes.
- As a plugin author, I want `open_pane: false` to be honoured consistently regardless of whether the command has placeholders, so the flag's contract is reliable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No pane for `a-r`** — Pressing `a-r` on an `in_review` item, entering a reason in the form, and submitting results in **no herdr pane being opened**; the audit-reject command runs in the background (detached `bash -c` with output captured to a per-run log file under `<tmpdir>/herdr-background-logs/`).
2. **Form-dialog parity** — The form-dialog `onSubmit` dispatch path in `worklist.ts` forwards `openPane` (and, when present, `onRefresh` and `focus`) to `onCommand` using the same arity rules as `executeResolvedCommand`/`resolveAndRouteCommand`, so placeholder shortcuts honour `open_pane: false` exactly like placeholder-free shortcuts.
3. **Default behaviour unchanged** — Shortcuts **without** `open_pane: false` (i.e. `open_pane` omitted or `true`) that trigger the form dialog still open a pane exactly as today (no regression for `c-q`, `u-s`, `u-t`, `c-n`, `P-p`, etc.).
4. **Background lifecycle preserved** — A background form-dialog dispatch still (a) fires the existing failure toast when the command exits non-zero, with the command, exit code/signal and an output excerpt (WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV), and (b) triggers the post-completion selection-list refresh via `onRefresh` (WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T).
5. **Test coverage** — A unit/integration test exercises the form-dialog dispatch path with `openPane === false` and asserts `onCommand` receives the flag (and `onRefresh`), plus a negative test asserting the default open-pane behaviour is unchanged.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (the "No-pane dispatch via `open_pane: false`" section), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **No new dispatch mechanism** — reuse the existing `open_pane: false` background execution path (`spawnBackgroundShell` / `spawnBackgroundPi` via `index.ts`'s `onCommand`). No new flag or config key is introduced.
- **Backward compatibility** — the fix must append `openPane`/`onRefresh`/`focus` only when they are `false`/present (matching the existing "append when explicitly set" rule in `resolveAndRouteCommand`), so 2-arg `onCommand` callers and pane-opening behaviour are byte-compatible.
- **Code Freeze guard preserved** — the form dialog's existing Code Freeze guard (`readCodeFreezeState().active && isImplementCommand(finalCmd)`) must remain intact.
- **Scope boundary** — adding `"open_pane": false` to other placeholder shortcuts (e.g. quick create `c-q`) is **out of scope** for this item and is tracked by the sibling item WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4; the generic root-cause fix here naturally benefits it once that flag is added.
- **Environment assumption** — herdr plugin runtime; the worklog data store is unaffected.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` already declares `"open_pane": false` for `a-r` (audit reject), `a-y` (audit approve), `u-p-l/m/h/c`, and `x-c`/`x-d`.
- `processChordInput` (`worklist.ts`) stores `chordState.resolvedOpenPane = entry.openPane ?? undefined` when a chord resolves.
- In the chord-complete handler, `openPane` (and `focus`) are read from `chordState`, cleared, and passed through `executeResolvedCommand(...)` to `dispatchChordCommand` → `resolveAndRouteCommand`, which forwards them to `onCommand` following strict arity rules.
- **The gap**: before reaching `executeResolvedCommand`, the chord handler checks `hasUnknownIdentifiers(command)` and, when true, constructs a `FormState` whose `onSubmit` calls `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model ?? undefined)` — dropping `openPane`, `onRefresh`, and `focus`. `a-r`'s `<reason>` placeholder always triggers this path, so the flag is lost and `index.ts` falls back to `shouldOpenPane = openPane ?? true`.
- The placeholder-free quiet shortcuts never hit the form dialog, which is why they already behave correctly.
- Existing tests cover `dispatchChordCommand`/`executeResolvedCommand` openPane plumbing (`worklist.test.ts` "openPane plumbing") and the audit reject compound command routing, but **not** the form-dialog dispatch path.

## Desired change

1. In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, in the form dialog's `onSubmit` handler, dispatch with the same arity/flag rules as `executeResolvedCommand`:
   - Resolve `<id>` and record the command as today.
   - Keep the Code Freeze guard as today.
   - Pass `openPane`, `onRefresh`, and `focus` to `opts.onCommand` (append only when `openPane`/`focus` are set / `onRefresh` is present) so `open_pane: false` and `focus: true` are honoured after form input.
2. Ensure the post-dispatch refresh logic (which currently suppresses the immediate refresh when `openPane === false` and relies on `onRefresh` at child exit) is consistent for the form-dialog path; if the form branch returns before the shared refresh block, trigger the equivalent refresh behaviour (or rely on the passed `onRefresh`).
3. Add regression tests for the form-dialog dispatch path (background `open_pane: false` forwarded; default unchanged).
4. Update `packages/herdr/README.md` to state that `open_pane: false` is honoured for shortcuts that trigger the placeholder form dialog (e.g. `a-r`).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — **Primary fix**: form dialog `onSubmit` dispatch (~line 6149) must forward `openPane`, `onRefresh`, and `focus` to `opts.onCommand`, mirroring `executeResolvedCommand`/`resolveAndRouteCommand`. Also verify the surrounding refresh logic for the form branch.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `a-r` already sets `"open_pane": false`; verify only (no change expected).

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Background dispatch path (`shouldOpenPane = openPane ?? true`, `spawnBackgroundShell`); no change expected, relevant context for verifying the flag reaches the handler.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — "Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane" (completed). Introduced the `open_pane: false` flag and the background dispatch path; this item fixes the flag being lost on the form-dialog path.

- **WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9** — "a-r (audit reject): reason containing apostrophe breaks shell command". Touches the same `a-r` `<reason>` form-submission path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix could expand into a broader "all shortcuts should optionally run in the background" review. **Mitigation**: keep this item to the form-dialog flag-plumbing bug; record further opportunities (e.g. defaulting forms to no-pane) as separate work items.
- **Arity/regression risk**: adding arguments to `opts.onCommand` in the form branch could break callers or tests that assert the 2-arg call. **Mitigation**: follow the existing "append only when explicitly set" rule already used by `resolveAndRouteCommand`, and add both positive and negative tests.
- **Refresh-timing risk**: if the form branch returns before the shared post-dispatch refresh block, the list may not refresh on completion. **Mitigation**: forward `onRefresh` and/or route the form branch through the shared refresh logic; cover with a test.
- **Assumption**: the operator's observed pane is caused by the form-dialog flag loss, not by a stale build or a project-local `shortcuts.json` override. Evidence: `a-r` has `open_pane: false`, the form path drops the flag, and no local override exists in this repo.
- **Assumption**: `a-r` should keep `open_pane: false` (the intended design per WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL); the fix restores the intended behaviour rather than changing the design.
- **Assumption**: the generic fix is preferable to an `a-r`-specific special case, and naturally covers future placeholder shortcuts with `open_pane: false`.

- **Q1**: "What is the actual root cause of the pane opening for `a-r`, given that `shortcuts.json` already sets `open_pane: false`?" — Answer (agent research): The `a-r` template contains the unknown placeholder `<reason>`, which routes the command through the placeholder form dialog. The form dialog's `onSubmit` handler calls `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model ?? undefined)` and drops the resolved `openPane` flag (`worklist.ts` ~line 6149), so `index.ts` falls back to opening a pane. Placeholder-free `open_pane: false` shortcuts (`a-y`, `u-p-*`, `x-c`, `x-d`) already work. Source: code inspection of `worklist.ts`, `form-dialog.ts`, `index.ts`, `shortcuts.json`, and `packages/herdr/README.md`.
- **Q2**: "Should the fix be generic (thread `openPane` through the form-dialog path) or an `a-r`-specific workaround?" — Answer (agent inference, documented assumption): Generic. The form-dialog path is the single shared point of failure for all placeholder shortcuts; a generic fix matches the existing `resolveAndRouteCommand` arity rules and avoids a special case. Final: generic (to be confirmed at implementation review).
- **Q3**: "Should `focus` and `onRefresh` also be threaded through the form-dialog path?" — Answer (agent inference): Yes for `onRefresh`, because background (`open_pane: false`) dispatches rely on the child-exit `onRefresh` to refresh the list (WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T) and the form branch currently cannot supply it. `focus` is moot when no pane opens, but forwarding it keeps parity with `executeResolvedCommand` and is harmless. - **Q4**: "Does adding `"open_pane": false` to the quick-create `c-q` shortcut belong in this item?" — Answer (agent inference): No. `c-q` currently has no `open_pane` flag and is tracked separately by WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4 ("Do not show pane for quick create"). # Intake Brief — Do not show pane for quick create (WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4)

**Headline**: The Herdr quick-create chord (`c` then `q`) always opens a visible
"Command Output" pane. Add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q` entry so the
`!!wl create` command runs detached in the background, with the selection list
refreshing on completion. The generic root-cause fix that lets *form-driven*
shortcuts honour `open_pane` is tracked separately by the blocking sibling
WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ; this item owns the `c q` opt-in, the quick-create
regression test, and end-to-end verification.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr selection list, the quick-create chord (`c` then `q`) dispatches
`!!wl create -t … -d … -p …` but always opens a visible "Command Output" pane.
The user must dismiss that pane after every quick create, even though the command
needs no visual confirmation and its result (a new work item) is visible in the
list itself. The per-shortcut `open_pane: false` feature that already makes other
shortcuts (audit approve/reject, priority updates, close/delete) run quietly is
not applied to the `c q` entry, so quick create never opts into background
execution.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** who create work items frequently via the `c q`
  chord and want the item created without a pane interrupting their browsing.

### User stories

- As a worklist user, when I press `c` then `q`, fill in the quick-create form
  and submit, I want the work item created **without a command-output pane
  opening**, so my flow is not interrupted and I can keep using the list.
- As a worklist user, I want the selection list to refresh once the background
  create completes, so the new item appears without me pressing refresh.
- As a user of any other shortcut, I want the pane-opening behaviour to be
  unchanged unless that shortcut explicitly sets `open_pane: false`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config opt-in** — The `c q` ("create quick") entry in
   `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` sets `"open_pane": false`.
2. **Background dispatch** — Submitting the quick-create form dispatches
   `!!wl create -t '<title>' -d '<description>' -p '<priority>'` with
   `openPane === false`, so no herdr pane is spawned; the command runs detached
   in the background with stdout/stderr captured to a per-run log (existing
   `spawnBackgroundShell` path in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`). This AC is
   enabled by the blocking sibling WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ (form-dialog flag
   propagation) and must be verified end-to-end once that item lands.
3. **Refresh on completion** — After the background `wl create` exits, the
   selection list refreshes (via the existing background `onRefresh` plumbing,
   WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T) so the newly created item appears without a manual or
   periodic refresh.
4. **Regression tests** — Automated tests assert: (a) the bundled `c q` entry
   is marked `open_pane: false`; and (b) submitting the quick-create form
   dispatches with `openPane === false` (no pane) — updating the existing
   `chord-quick-create.test.ts` assertion that currently expects the 2-arg
   pane-opening call.
5. **Default unchanged** — Other, non-opted-in shortcuts (including other
   form-driven ones) still open a pane exactly as today.
6. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (the "No-pane
   dispatch via `open_pane: false`" section), and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
7. **Full suite** — The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Depends on WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** — the form-dialog dispatch path must
  forward `openPane`/`onRefresh` before a form-driven `c q` opt-in can take
  effect. This item must not duplicate that `worklist.ts` fix; it adds the
  config and verifies/tests the resulting behaviour.
- **Default unchanged:** shortcuts without `open_pane` must keep opening a pane
  exactly as today; the change only affects entries that opt in.
- **Single-instance refresh:** the completion refresh is scoped to the
  dispatching TUI instance (fire-and-forget, non-blocking); no global watcher
  and no cross-instance effects.
- **Feedback:** the background path's existing behaviour is retained — a stderr
  line with the log path at dispatch, and a toast only on non-zero exit; no new
  visible pane or modal is introduced.
- **Surgical change:** the change is the one-line config opt-in plus tests; do
  not alter the `open_pane` schema or the
  `spawnBackgroundShell`/`spawnBackgroundPi` implementations.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — the `c q` entry has no `open_pane` key,
  so dispatch defaults to opening a pane. Other quiet shortcuts (`a-y`, `a-r`,
  `u-p-*`, `x-c`, `x-d`) already set `"open_pane": false`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the form-submit closures currently drop the
  resolved `openPane` flag (calling `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model)`), so even
  a configured `open_pane: false` would be ignored for form-driven shortcuts.
  This is **fixed by WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** (out of scope here).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — already routes `openPane === false` `!!`
  commands to `spawnBackgroundShell` and wires `onExit` → `onRefresh`; no change
  expected.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — already parses `open_pane` into
  `openPane`; no change expected.

## Desired change

1. Add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q` entry in `shortcuts.json`.
2. Add `'c,q'` to the expected no-pane set in the shortcut-config regression
   test.
3. Update the quick-create form test to assert the background dispatch
   (third arg `false` + `onRefresh`) rather than the current 2-arg
   pane-opening call.
4. Once WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ lands, verify end-to-end that `c q` creates the
   item with no pane and that the list refreshes on completion.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Dependency risk:** until WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ lands, the config opt-in alone
  will not suppress the pane; the quick-create test would need the sibling fix
  to pass. Mitigation: record the blocking relationship and sequence
  implementation after the sibling.
- **Risk — silent failure:** a background create that fails is only visible via
  a failure toast + log. Mitigation: rely on the existing
  `notifyBackgroundFailure` path; no new mechanism.
- **Assumption:** the list refresh on completion is sufficient feedback for a
  created item; no explicit success toast is required. Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`onRefresh` on background exit).
- **Scope-creep risk:** incidental improvements to the quick-create form
  (e.g. validation, issue-type selection), or applying `open_pane: false` to
  other form shortcuts, are out of scope and should be recorded as separate work
  items rather than folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q`
  ("create quick") entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/chord-quick-create.test.ts` — update the submit assertion
  to expect the background dispatch (third arg `false` + `onRefresh`) instead of
  the current 2-arg call; assert no pane is opened.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — add `'c,q'` to the expected
  `open_pane: false` set in the "quiet state-change shortcuts" test.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — **not changed here**; the form-dialog flag
  propagation is delivered by WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document that `c q` is a quiet (no-pane)
  shortcut, if the README enumerates them.

## Related work

- **WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** — Don't open pane for recording reviews. **Blocking
  sibling**: fixes the shared form-dialog dispatch path so form-driven
  shortcuts honour `open_pane: false`; its scope boundary explicitly defers the
  `c q` opt-in to this item.
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — Add per-shortcut option to control whether a
  shortcut opens a command pane. The parent feature that introduced
  `open_pane: false`; its AC5 seeded the `a-y` entry but did not cover
  form-driven shortcuts.
- **WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T** — Refresh the selection list when background
  (no-pane) shortcut commands complete. Supplies the `onRefresh` hook this item
  relies on (AC3).
- **WL-0MTCLB50D0026YA7** — Support multiple create options. Introduced the
  `c n` / `c q` chords and the quick-create form.
- **WL-0MU9LJPI5000HOR4** — Update shortcuts.json: replace c shortcut with c-n
  and c-q chords. Introduced the `c q` quick-create chord entry that this item
  makes background.
- **WL-0MLSDIRLA0BXRCDB** — Add /create OpenCode command for creating work
  items from TUI. Related create-work-item-from-TUI work (different surface,
  same user flow).
- **WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N** — Herdr selection list requires double dispatch for
  priority update to reflect. Documents the background-dispatch refresh
  suppression this item's AC3 builds on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: (No clarifying questions asked.) — The seed context was judged sufficient:
  the desired behaviour ("do not open this pane, do the work in the
  background") is explicit, and the repo already provides the `open_pane: false`
  feature and background-dispatch/refresh plumbing. Source: agent evaluation of
  `WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4` description and repo inspection.
- Q: Is this a duplicate of the form-path fix in WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ? — Answer:
  Partial overlap only. The sibling fixes the generic form-dialog flag
  propagation and explicitly scopes the `c q` opt-in out to this item
  (WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ, "Scope boundary"). This item therefore covers the
  `c q` config, its regression test, and end-to-end verification, and is
  recorded as blocked-by the sibling. Source: `wl show
  WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ`; `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
- Q: Should the quick create still surface the created work-item ID? —
  Research: the background path writes command output (including the new ID) to
  a per-run log file and shows a toast only on failure; the list refreshes on
  completion, making the new item visible. Assumption: this is acceptable and
  matches the "background" intent. Source: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
  (`spawnBackgroundShell`, `notifyBackgroundFailure`, `onRefresh`).
- Q: Should shortcuts without `open_pane` change? — Answer: No; the default
  (open a pane) is unchanged. Source: WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL AC4.
- Open question: none.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** – Don't open pane for recording reviews (open)
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** – Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane (completed)
- **WL-0MU9LJPI5000HOR4** – Update shortcuts.json: replace c shortcut with c-n and c-q chords (completed)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, add, adds (+244 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, adds, affects, agent, alone (+216 more)

## Goal

In the herdr selection list, items with `status = in-progress` and `stage = in_review` must be included in the mandatory in_review set (always shown regardless of `browseItemCount`), just like `completed`/`in_review` items.

## Problem

Items being re-worked after review feedback keep `stage = in_review` but flip `status` to `in-progress` (per the project workflow, WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW). The smart-selection mandatory set only matches `status === 'completed' && stage === 'in_review'`:

- `smart-selection.ts`: `isMandatoryItem()` and the `reviews` filter in `selectWorkItems()` require `status === 'completed'`.
- `fetcher.ts`: `reviewQueueArgs()` / `fetchMandatorySubsets()` fetch `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, so in-progress/in_review items aren't in the guaranteed subset at all.

As a result an in-progress/in_review item can be dropped from the default list when the `browseItemCount` window fills — it only survives as a capped "others" row. Only the stage-filtered `/wl in_review` view shows them reliably.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `isMandatoryItem()` returns true for `status = in-progress` + `stage = in_review` (as well as `completed` + `in_review`, and critical).
- AC2: `selectWorkItems()` always includes in_progress/in_review items in the guaranteed review set (unbounded by `browseItemCount`), without double-counting items already in the critical set.
- AC3: `fetchMandatorySubsets()`/`reviewQueueArgs()` fetches `--status completed,in-progress` for the in_review mandatory subset so the fetch layer matches the selection-layer guarantee.
- AC4: The duplicative "another copy lives in the Pi TUI Worklog extension" note in `smart-selection.ts` is corrected — that copy was removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N, so only the herdr copy (and the core `wl next` grouping duplication noted in `grouping.ts`) remains.
- AC5: All tests pass (update `smart-selection.test.ts`, fetcher tests, grouping regressions as needed; add coverage for in-progress/in_review included in the mandatory set).

## Goal

Actively-worked work items (status = in-progress) must be guaranteed a place in the herdr default selection list even when the mandatory review queue saturates `browseItemCount`.

## Problem

`fetchNextItems(count)` → `selectWorkItems(merged, count)` guarantees critical and in_review items are always shown (unbounded by `browseItemCount`), but every other item (including actively-worked `in-progress` items, which render in the "Group N" section) competes for the capped "others" budget:

```
othersLimit = max(0, browseItemCount - (criticals.length + reviews.length))
```

When the review queue is deep (root in_review count ≥ browseItemCount), `othersLimit` drops to 0 and ALL "others" are cut — an actively-worked item (e.g. `status=in-progress, stage=plan_complete`) vanishes from the default list even though `wl next --include-in-progress` returns it first. Observed with WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX (22 mandatory reviews vs browseItemCount 20 → 0 others shown). Additionally, `wl next -n N` hard-caps at 32 items, so a low-priority in-progress item can fall outside the top-N base window altogether.

Actively-worked items are the producer's most important real-time signal ("what am I working on right now") — losing them from the list is worse than showing a slightly longer list.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `selectWorkItems()` always includes items with `status = in-progress` (regardless of stage, not `done`) in the returned list — unbounded by `browseItemCount`, deduplicated against critical/in_review items (counts once when an item matches multiple criteria).
- AC2: `isMandatoryItem()` returns true for `status = in-progress` items (plus the existing critical and in_progress/in_review cases).
- AC3: Ordering within the mandatory additions: criticals first, then in_review reviews, then actively-worked in-progress items, then capped others — so the Group N (actively-worked) section still renders ahead of "Other" after regrouping.
- AC4: `fetchMandatorySubsets()` also fetches actively-worked root items explicitly (`wl list --status in-progress --root-only`), so an in-progress item is surfaced by `fetchNextItems()` even when it falls outside the `wl next` top-N window and even when review-queue depth pushes `othersLimit` to 0. `fetchReviewQueueState` is unaffected (its query stays shared with the mandatory review subset — the in-progress fetch is a separate, additional query).
- AC5: All tests pass, including new coverage for the review-queue-saturation scenario, the in-progress item outside the `wl next` window, and the overlap cases.
data.title: Herdr selection list: always show actively-worked in-progress items even when review queue saturates the window
