The Herdr worklist selection list calls wl next to populate its results. wl next excludes dependency-blocked items by default (filterCandidates removes them unless includeBlocked is true). This means the Herdr selection list never shows dependency-blocked items, even though the user may need to see what is blocking their backlog.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. The Herdr worklist selection list includes dependency-blocked items alongside open and in-progress items.
2. Blocked items are rendered with a visible indicator (status icon) so their state is clear.
3. The change is confined to the fetchNextItems invocation in fetcher.ts - no other callers of wl next are affected.
4. Unit tests cover the new --include-blocked flag in the args array.

Notes:
The change adds --include-blocked to the wl next args in fetchNextItems() (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts). status=blocked items were already included by wl next (the pipeline only penalises them with -10000); the gap is dependency-blocked items that are excluded entirely. Blocked items will rank low (penalised) by default scoring, so they appear at the bottom of the list.

data.description:
Inconsistency between the Herdr in_review stage filter and the ship release gate:

- The ship skill queries "wl list --stage in_review" with NO status filter (check-audit-gate.js, check-final-validation.js, generate-changelog.js), so a status=blocked item in the in_review stage (e.g. WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P) IS seen by the release gate and blocks the release.
- The Herdr in_review stage filter (fetchItemsByStage -> STAGE_STATUS.in_review = "completed,in-progress,open") EXCLUDES status=blocked items, so the same item never appears in the in_review filtered selection list.

The user-facing symptom: an in_review item that blocks the release is invisible in the /wl review view, so the selection list and the release gate disagree about what is in the review queue.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want the in_review filter to show every root item the ship release gate sees in in_review, so the selection list and the release gate agree on the review queue.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchItemsByStage(in_review) issues a wl list query whose status filter includes blocked alongside completed/in-progress/open (verified by a unit test asserting the exec args).
2. A status=blocked root item at stage=in_review appears in the stage-filtered in_review list.
3. Other stages keep their existing status rules unchanged.
4. The stage-filter documentation (STAGE_STATUS comment in fetcher.ts, worklist.ts doc, packages/herdr/README.md) reflects that in_review includes blocked items.
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- Root cause: STAGE_STATUS.in_review omits blocked. The project workflow (AGENTS.md, WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW) documented blocked as excluded, but the release gate does not exclude it — the exclusion makes release-blocking items invisible in the review filter.
- Fix: STAGE_STATUS.in_review = completed,in-progress,open,blocked. discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
data.title: Herdr in_review filter hides blocked items that the release gate treats as release-blocking

data.description:
Follow-up to WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2. Adding --include-blocked to wl next made blocked items ELIGIBLE, but the default worklist still does not show a low-ranked blocked item such as WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P (status=blocked, stage=in_review, rank ~35 of 52):

- The base feed is `wl next -n <browseItemCount>` (default 20): the ranked #35 item is cut before it ever enters the pool.
- The mandatory subsets (critical, completed/in_review, in-progress) do not include status=blocked items, so smart selection cannot surface it either.
- Only the /wl review stage filter shows it (fixed in WL-0MV70XY6D008013C).

Per the operator: an in_review item blocks the release, so it must either appear in the list or not be in_review. It IS in_review, therefore it must appear in the DEFAULT list too.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want status=blocked root items always visible in the default worklist (like critical / in_review-completed / in-progress items), so release-blocking work can never be hidden by ranking or count caps.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchMandatorySubsets() fetches status=blocked root-only items (wl list --status blocked --root-only) alongside the existing mandatory subsets.
2. selectWorkItems / isMandatoryItem treat status=blocked as mandatory: a blocked root item is always shown regardless of browseItemCount and rank.
3. The default worklist shows a low-ranked blocked in_review root item (regression test).
4. Non-blocked items keep existing behaviour (order, caps).
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
- Also requires the user to close/reopen (or restart the herdr server to respawn) the worklist pane for new code to load: tsx runs without --watch, so an already-open pane keeps the old code.

# Intake Brief: Herdr downtime audit claim leaves item in-progress/in_review; failed audit strands review-queue items

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher's audit-tier pre-dispatch CAS claim flips a `completed`/`in_review` item's status to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid state that the audit runner's own inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` table rejects. When the audit then fails (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure), the runner's failure-restore coerces the hybrid to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding the item one step down — off the review queue, out of the audit tier's selection, and out of the release gate's visibility.

## Users

- **Operator** (runs herdr downtime dispatch): wants audit auto-dispatch to be transparent — no item should silently change state as a side effect of being audited.
- **Producer/reviewer**: wants every `in_review` item to stay on the review queue (observable via `completed`/`in_review`) until a genuine audit verdict or manual action moves it, so infra failures never invisibly remove work from review.
- **Auto-dispatched audit agent** (`/skill:audit <id>`): wants pre-flight guard and pre-audit state capture to see the true pre-claim state (`completed`/`in_review`), not the dispatcher's claim artifact.

User stories:
- As an operator, when herdr auto-dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item and the audit fails, the item must remain `completed`/`in_review` so a re-run or manual review can still proceed.
- As a producer, I want no failed audit to ever strand an item at `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, invisible to the review queue and the audit tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the herdr audit tier dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item, the item's observable state (via `wl show`) never becomes `in-progress`/`in_review` as a dispatch artifact — the claim is status- and stage-neutral (or restores the pre-claim state as the single visible state while the audit runs only where the runner itself manages the lifecycle).

- After a failed/interrupted herdr-dispatched audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure, SIGKILL, pane kill), the item is verified back at `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` readback — never `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, and never left `in_progress`.

- The audit runner's failure-restore and abort-recovery (SIGKILL state-file) paths restore `completed`/`in_review` for review-queue items, including when the captured pre-audit state is the herdr claim hybrid — no coercion to `plan_complete`. Covered by unit + integration tests.

- Double-dispatch protection (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1: exactly one concurrent pane wins the claim) is preserved; the alternative claim mechanism has its own race-safety test.

- The existing `in-progress`/`in_review` transitional exception in the wl validator (`src/status-stage-validation.ts`) is retained or tightened only in step with the chosen fix (never removed while herdr can still create the hybrid); regression tests for the validator remain green.

- **Testing/validation criterion:** all of the above are covered by meaningful tests (unit + an integration-style dispatch→failed-audit→restore scenario); the full project test suite passes with the changes.

- **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `AGENTS.md` (claim pattern), and any relevant skill docs (`/skill:audit` README note on CAS claims).

- **Suite criterion:** full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub `tests/` + `packages/herdr`); cross-repo audit-runner tests in the owning project where the fix lands.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary (decided 2026-10-14):** `audit_runner.py` lives in the shared skills install sourced from the SorraAgents repo (`skill/audit`), not this repo. Changes there happen via that repo's own work items (SA work item), linked from here as `Blocked-by`. This bug is the tracking/verification item.
- The dispatch-failure rollback path (`rollbackClaimWorkItem`) already restores `completed`/`in_review` for audit (fetcher.ts `rollbackClaimWorkItem`); it must keep working and be covered.
- `needsProducerReview` removal and the assignee-based scheduling hold are out of scope for the *immediate* bug fix — they belong to epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (Option A follow-on). This item must not depend on that epic landing.
- Keep the fix surgical: no behaviour change to the other tiers' claims (they legitimately claim `open` items as in_progress) or to the review-queue depth gate.
- The audit runner's own entry claim (in_progress) and the pre-flight guard (needs `--force` for in_progress items) remain as-is unless the chosen fix removes the need for `--force`; if the claim becomes status-neutral, the pre-flight guard no longer trips and the audit no longer needs `--force` — that is desirable, not a regression.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` `claimWorkItem` (L1197) always sets `--status in_progress`; `TIER_EXPECTED.audit = {status:'completed', stage:'in_review'}` (downtime-worker.ts:2385) is only the CAS guard.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchClaimedTier` (L2943) claims with the tier expectation, then marker, then spawn; rollback on marker/spawn failure restores via `rollbackClaimWorkItem` with the tier's expected state (completed/in_review for audit).
- The wl validator (`src/status-stage-validation.ts`, compiled `dist/status-stage-validation.js:36-48`) already permits `in-progress`/`in_review` as a documented transitional exception for exactly this audit path.
- The audit runner's separate inlined table (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT`, L11894) lacks that exception, so `_coerce_valid_status_stage` (L11931-11937) coerces `in_review → plan_complete` on failure-restore.
- The audit runner success path (`wl update --status completed --stage in_review`) already returns the item to the review queue; only the failure/interrupt path is broken.
- Related completed work proves the edges: WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH (retired `in_progress` *stage* claim), SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1 (invalid pre-audit combo coercion in audit runner), SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY (pre-flight guard).

## Desired change

Chosen approach (producer decision): **Option A — make the audit-tier claim status-/stage-neutral** so the item stays `completed`/`in_review` through the herdr dispatch claim; the audit runner then captures the true pre-claim state and its failure-restore returns `completed`/`in_review` naturally. The full update is delivered through the existing epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (status-neutral assignee CAS claim for the audit tier + `needsProducerReview` re-homing), which this item tracks as the root-cause bug. If the epic's full scope cannot proceed, a minimal audit_runner-side mapping (`in-progress`/`in_review` → `completed`/`in_review` on the restore paths, in the owning repo) is the agreed fallback (Option B) but is not the primary path.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `claimWorkItem`: add a status-neutral claim path for the audit tier (produce a `--if-assignee ""`-guarded or equivalent non-status-flipping claim) — needs `wl update --if-assignee` support in `src/commands/update.ts`.
- `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` — `--if-assignee` CAS guard support; transitional-exception handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `TIER_EXPECTED` / `dispatchClaimedTier`: wire the audit tier's claim to the status-neutral path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/claim.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — race-safety + failed-audit-restore regression tests.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents repo) — verify failure-restore + abort-recovery restore `completed`/`in_review`; add the hybrid mapping if the herdr claim still flips status at the time of capture.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents repo) — cross-repo regression tests if the audit-runner mapping changes.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `AGENTS.md` (claim pattern), and the `/skill:audit` docs — update the claim/transitional-exception documentation per AC7.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed):** Option A (status-neutral claim) is the primary path and is delivered through epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ; this item tracks the root-cause bug and verifies it. If the epic is descoped, the agreed fallback is the audit-runner mapping (Option B).
- **Assumption:** the status-neutral claim requires new `wl update` CAS support (`--if-assignee`) because `--if-status`/`--if-stage` alone cannot make a no-op write exclusive. If that API is rejected, the fallback Option B must be used instead.
- **Risk — assignee residue (P1/P2 in the epic):** clearing discipline and rollback paths must clear the assignee or items ossify as permanently unclaimable. Highest-impact failure mode; the epic owns the mitigation, but this item's verification must assert the audit re-runs after failure.
- **Risk — sync regression guard (P3):** clearing an assignee cross-root may be refused without `--accept-regressions`, resurrecting cleared claims. Must be documented/decided in the epic.
- **Risk — new blocker semantics (P4):** any non-empty assignee becomes a dispatch blocker. Intended as a scheduling hold, but every skill that sets an assignee must clear it on session end; otherwise auto-dispatch silently stops for those items.
- **Risk — validator exception drift:** the wl validator's transitional exception and the audit runner's inlined table are duplicated logic that can drift again; add a test that pins the pair, or centralise.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the pull to also remove `needsProducerReview` and re-home the release gate is high, but that is epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ scope. Any extra opportunity discovered during this item is recorded as a linked work item, not absorbed here.
- **Failure mode if partially fixed:** changing only the herdr claim without the audit runner's abort-recovery path leaves SIGKILL strands at a hybrid state; both paths are covered by the ACs.

## Related work

- Epic **WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ** (Option A: status-neutral assignee CAS claim for audit tier + remove needsProducerReview) — this item is a **tracking/verification umbrella** that **depends-on** the epic (Blocked-by) and is auto-unblocked when the epic completes; the epic carries the full Option A design incl. P1–P8 analysis. Dependency direction corrected 2026-10-14 (producer Q-C).
- **WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH** (retired in_progress stage claim fix) — completed; same claim path, different trigger.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** (CAS claim RCA) — completed; design point 1 this fix must preserve.
- **SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY** (pre-flight guard) — completed; interacts with the audit claim state.
- **SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1** (audit_runner invalid pre-audit combo coercion) — completed; the coercion this bug hits.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** (conditional claim + marker exclusion impl) — completed.
- **WL-0MUWKGW9W004QXQZ** (claim skip for done) — completed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fix approach — (A) herdr status-neutral claim (epic scope), (B) audit_runner restore fix, (C) staged B-now/A-later — which?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): **A** — the status-neutral claim redesign; the epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ is the delivery vehicle. Source: interactive intake reply.
- Q2: "Repo boundary — cross-repo acceptable (audit-runner fix in SorraAgents) or ContextHub-only?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): **(a) cross-repo acceptable** — audit_runner changes land in its owning repo's work items, linked from here. Source: interactive intake reply.

## Effort and risk (preliminary)

- **Effort:** Large (cross-repo: herdr claim redesign + `wl update` CAS API + audit-runner lifecycle verification). The narrow fallback (Option B) is Small; the primary Option A path is Large.
- **Risk:** High — touches the CAS claim that prevents duplicate dispatch (WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT), a shared lifecycle owner in another repo, and cross-root sync semantics.

## RM summary (research)

Confirmed the wl validator already allows the hybrid as a documented transitional exception and the audit runner's separate table does not; confirmed the audit runner owns the exit-side lifecycle and lives outside this repo; confirmed no completed item duplicates this bug (SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1 fixed the coercion mechanics generally, not the dispatch-claim hybrid); verified `--if-assignee` is not yet a `wl update` flag, so a status-neutral claim requires either that flag or an equivalent CAS mechanism.

# Intake Brief — Change medium priority icon (WL-0MV7WQTJ9003SAV1)

**Headline**: The medium priority icon renders as 📋, identical to the plan_complete stage icon. Change the medium priority icon to 🟨 (yellow square) in both the CLI theme and the shared icon module so priority and stage remain visually distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

Medium priority work items render the 📋 (clipboard) icon in the CLI and TUI/herdr list rows — the exact same glyph used for the `plan_complete` stage icon. A medium-priority item at `plan_complete` stage therefore shows two adjacent identical glyphs, making it impossible to tell priority from stage at a glance. Change the priority glyph (not the stage glyph).

## Users

- **Worklog CLI users** — `wl list`/`wl show` rows colour-code and icon-code priority.
  - *As a developer scanning a work-item list, I want the medium priority icon to differ from the plan_complete stage icon, so I can distinguish priority from stage at a glance.*
- **Herdr / Pi TUI users** — the selection-list icon prefix shows priority and stage together.
  - *As a TUI user, I want each field to have a unique glyph, so the icon prefix remains scannable.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The medium priority icon in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`PRIORITY_ICONS.medium`) renders as 🟨 (U+1F7E8) in icon mode; the text fallback `[MED ]` is unchanged.
2. The medium priority icon in `src/theme.ts` (`PRIORITY_ICON.medium`) renders as 🟨, keeping CLI/shared parity.
3. The `plan_complete` stage icon remains 📋 in both files — only the priority glyph changes.
4. Unit tests asserting the medium **priority** glyph are updated to expect 🟨 and pass: `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` (priority assertions at lines ~59 and ~79 only — the `plan_complete` **stage** assertions at lines ~333/~356 stay 📋) and `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` (expected-priority map at line ~329, the no-priority negative regex at line ~354, and the `medium` prefix assertions at lines ~392–393). `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts` contain **no** medium-priority glyph assertions; their `📋` assertions are stage-based (`plan_complete`) and must remain unchanged. (full project test suite passes)
5. `docs/icons-design.md` is updated: the priority icons table shows 🟨 for medium, the column-0 list-row legend ("Priority icon | `🚨` critical, `⭐` high, `📋` medium, `🐢` low") shows 🟨, and the "Colour association" note below it is adjusted to match (colour over glyph; 🟡 is not the medium glyph).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Visual-only change.** No data-model, persistence, or file-path changes.
- Both canonical definitions must change together: `src/theme.ts` (CLI) and `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (herdr/shared). No new drift between them.
- Text fallbacks (`[MED ]`, `[MED]`) and `noIcons` behaviour are unchanged — only the emoji/icon mode glyph changes.
- The replacement glyph must not collide with any other in-use icon (stage, risk, effort, status). 🟨 is currently unused across the icon set.
- The chosen glyph must be terminal-safe (single-width/colour emoji with wide terminal support).

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:78` — `PRIORITY_ICONS.medium = '\u{1F4CB}'` (📋), colliding with `STAGE_ICONS.plan_complete` (line 58, 📋).
- `src/theme.ts:54` — `PRIORITY_ICON.medium = '\u{1F4CB}'` (📋), colliding with `plan_complete` at line 280 (📋).
- `docs/icons-design.md` documents 📋 as the medium-priority glyph in the § Priority Icons table.
- Tests assert `\u{1F4CB}` for `priorityIcon('medium')`: `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` (lines 59, 79) and `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` (expected-priority map line 329, no-priority negative regex line 354, `getIconPrefix` assertions lines 392–393); stage `plan_complete` assertions (`tests/unit/icons.test.ts` lines 333/356, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` lines 1093/1117) are unchanged.
- The risk medium icon is 🟡 (yellow circle, U+1F7E1) — distinct from the chosen 🟨 (yellow square).

## Desired change

1. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `PRIORITY_ICONS.medium`: `'\u{1F4CB}'` → `'\u{1F7E8}'` (🟨), with an updated comment.
2. `src/theme.ts` — `PRIORITY_ICON.medium`: `'\u{1F4CB}'` → `'\u{1F7E8}'` (🟨), with an updated comment.
3. Update the affected glyph assertions in the four test files above to `'\u{1F7E8}'`.
4. Update `docs/icons-design.md` § Priority Icons table and its colour-association note.
5. `plan_complete` (📋) is intentionally left unchanged everywhere.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `PRIORITY_ICONS.medium` changes to 🟨 (U+1F7E8).
- `src/theme.ts` — `PRIORITY_ICON.medium` changes to 🟨 (U+1F7E8).
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — medium-priority glyph assertions updated (lines ~58–59, ~79).
- `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` — medium-priority expectations updated (lines ~329, ~354, ~392–393); `plan_complete` stage assertions unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — no medium-priority glyph assertions exist; its `📋` assertions are `plan_complete` stage assertions and stay unchanged (touch only if a medium-priority assertion is found).
- `docs/icons-design.md` — priority icons table, column-0 list-row legend (~line 359) + colour-association note updated (no new collision documented).

## Related work

- **WL-0MNAGKMG5002L3XJ** — "Icons for priority and status" (completed). Origin of the current icon set; introduced 📋 for medium priority alongside 📋 for plan_complete.
- **WL-0MTQYTA20009YXBT** — "Add a priority icon to the selection list" (completed). Wired priority icons into herdr's selection list.
- **WL-0MUBECS6S0047UYC** — "Update getIconPrefix to include priority icon" (completed). Built the icon prefix that renders both priority and stage glyphs.
- **WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6** — priority→colour mapping scheme (medium = yellow), referenced in docs/icons-design.md.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Residual colour similarity (risk)**: 🟨 (yellow square) is close in colour to the risk-medium 🟡 (yellow circle). **Mitigation**: distinct shape (square vs circle); risk icons appear in the pipe-separated info bar while priority icons appear in the list-row icon prefix — the same position-based disambiguation already documented for critical 🚨 overlapping risk 🚨 in `docs/icons-design.md` §12 note.
- **Glyph rendering (risk)**: some terminal fonts may render 🟨 as a yellow square or fall back; the square glyph has wide Unicode/emoji support and is no more exotic than the other colour-square icons already in use (🟢/🟡/🟩).
- **Scope-creep risk**: only the medium priority glyph changes. Other icon collisions or "redesign the whole icon set" ideas are recorded as separate work items, not this item. Known adjacent opportunities: 🟡 risk-medium vs 🟨 priority-medium colour similarity (documented, accepted), effort-diamond vs other diamond shapes.
- **Assumption**: both the CLI (`src/theme.ts`) and shared (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) definitions are in scope (operator confirmed "change the priority one" — i.e. the shared/priority glyph; parity requires the CLI copy too).
- **Assumption**: `plan_complete` keeps 📋; the stage vocabulary is the stable axis.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The medium priority icon (📋) collides with the plan_complete stage icon (📋). Which replacement glyph should medium priority use? Options: 1) 🟨 yellow square (U+1F7E8) — recommended (matches medium→yellow colour association, distinct shape, currently unused); 2) 🔸 orange diamond (U+1F538); 3) ⚖️ balance scale (U+2696); 4) 📌 pushpin (U+1F4CC); 5) other." — Answer (operator rgardler): "1" (🟨). Source: interactive reply in intake interview. Final: yes — `\u{1F7E8}`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT1C2E0K001CTJ7** – Update tests: point at theme.ts, add wrapper parity test (completed)
- **WL-0MUUAEDAU001GT1L** – a-r (audit reject) should not change work item priority (completed)
- **WL-0MV1CZFAC001IX5V** – [test-failure] delta export of a handful of changed records over a 2000-item store completes ≤ 2500ms — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: change, complete, icon, medium, one (+2 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: change, complete, icon, medium, one (+2 more)
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` — matched: change, complete, icon, medium, one (+2 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-14 (plan skill, skip path — effort Extra Small / risk Low): AC4 rewritten to remove a contradiction with AC3 (it named `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts`, whose `📋` assertions are `plan_complete` **stage** assertions, not medium-priority glyph assertions, and which contain no medium-priority glyph assertions at all). AC5 extended to name the column-0 list-row legend in `docs/icons-design.md`. "Existing state" and "Key Files (predicted)" updated for line-level accuracy in `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` and to drop the untouched `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts`. No change to intent or scope.

# Epic: Option A — status-neutral assignee CAS claim for the audit tier + remove `needsProducerReview`

## Problem statement

When the herdr downtime worker auto-dispatches an audit of a completed/in_review item, its CAS claim flips `status` to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid `in-progress`/`in_review` pair that the audit runner's failure-restore path cannot represent — so a failed audit (Phase 2 timeout, infra failure, killed pane) coerces the item to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding it off the review queue (root cause: WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL). Separately, `needsProducerReview` has grown into a magic DB flag whose two roles — blocking auto-dispatch and gating the ship release — need to be re-homed onto the assignee field so the flag and its whole surface (`wl reviewed`, CLI/API filters, herdr icon/logic, audit runner, ship gate) can be removed.

## Users

- **Operator** running herdr downtime dispatch. Story: "When an auto-dispatched audit of a completed/in_review item fails, I want the item to stay completed/in_review — on the review queue and re-selectable — so broken audits never strand work in in-progress/plan_complete."
- **Producer** reviewing work. Story: "I want an explicit, per-item way to pause automatic scheduling (assign the item to me) that does not rely on a magic DB flag, and I want a release gate that still stops me from shipping unreviewed work."
- **Agent tier / pane** competing for the same item. Story: "Exactly one concurrent claim must win, even when the claim does not change status."

## Approach (Option A, per root cause fix-options)

Make the audit-tier claim **status-neutral**: the claim's CAS becomes the **assignee** instead of `status`. Add `--if-assignee <value>` to `wl update` (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` CAS, same machinery as `updateIfMatches`), then the audit-tier claim writes:

```
wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""
```

The item stays completed/in_review throughout — no hybrid state is ever created, so the audit runner's pre-audit capture and failure-restore are correct (no `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` coercion to plan_complete). Exactly one pane still wins (CAS on the guarded fields), preserving the WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT RC-1 single-claim guarantee.

Remove `needsProducerReview` from the database and re-home its two roles onto the assignee field:
- **Scheduling hold:** assign to the producer ⇒ no tier claims it ⇒ no auto-dispatch.
- **Release gate:** an item assigned to the producer means "the producer owns it"; `check-final-validation.js` blocks release until such items have been reviewed (audit verdict 'Ready to close: Yes').

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl update` supports `--if-assignee` CAS (atomic, single-winner; unit + integration tests).
- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
- [ ] Regression test: herdr dispatch claim → simulated audit Phase-2 failure → item back at completed/in_review, re-selectable (no in-progress/plan_complete, no needsProducerReview-column dependency).
- [ ] Failed dispatch (marker-write-failed / spawn-failed) clears assignee and leaves item re-selectable.
- [ ] Success path clears assignee; legacy residue cleared by a one-time migration/script; audit re-runs still dispatch.
- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
- [ ] `needsProducerReview` column removed from DB; `wl reviewed` and all `--needs-producer-review` CLI/API options removed; no references left in src/, packages/, skill/, .pi/skills/.
- [ ] Ship release gate re-homed onto the assignee hold without weakening release safety (check-final-validation.js updated + tested).
- [ ] Sync regression guard behaviour for assignee documented/decided and tested cross-root.
- [ ] Full test suite passes; CLI.md / docs updated; AGENTS.md claim pattern updated.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo skill boundary:** `audit_runner.py`, `status_lifecycle.py`, and the ship gate scripts (`check-final-validation.js`, `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`) live in the **SorraAgents** skill tree (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`). AGENTS.md forbids editing `skill/` dirs without explicit instruction; changes there must be tracked as SA work items linked from here (see bug intake question 2 — repo boundary, still awaiting producer answer).
- **No hybrid status/stage write:** the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`; the old dual-set claim is the bug's source.
- **Race safety preserved:** the `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback must be similarly guarded (`--if-assignee <agent>`) so only this claim's state is reverted.
- **Assignee residue is a live problem:** 698 completed items and 7 in_review items already carry `assignee=Map` (P1); the legacy-cleanup is table-stakes or the queue ossifies.
- **Sync regression guard:** `assignee` is merge-participating and `'Map' → ''` is refused as a regression on other roots unless the guard is changed or `--accept-regressions` used (P3).
- **Migration history preserved:** the add-migration (20260210-add-needsProducerReview) stays for history; a new drop-migration removes the column.
- **Docs/conventions:** AGENTS.md claim pattern, herdr README downtime-dispatcher docs, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, CLI.md, icons-design.md, CHANGELOG updated.
- **UK English, Markdown descriptions, wl is source of truth** per project rules.
- **Push only to `dev`** per push policy.

## Existing state

- `wl update` supports `--if-status` / `--if-stage` CAS (used by `claimWorkItem` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`, which flips `--status in_progress --assignee <agent>`); no `--if-assignee` field exists yet.
- `claimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1197) and `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1268) implement the dispatch claim/rollback; `downtime-worker.ts` (`dispatchClaimedTier`, `rollbackClaimForFailure`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, all `select*` functions) consumes them.
- `needsProducerReview` is stored in the DB (column, migration 20260210-add-needsProducerReview), exposed via `wl reviewed` (src/commands/reviewed.ts), `wl update --needs-producer-review`, `wl list/search/next` filters, api.ts query param, cli-types, persistent-store schema/jsonl/sync.
- The audit runner (SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `--needs-producer-review yes` on 'yes' verdicts and never clears `--assignee ""` (P1). Its failure-restore path has an inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` that coerces `in_review → plan_complete`.
- The ship release gate (`skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`) blocks release on `needsProducerReview === true` items.
- `interview.ts` explains/clears the flag (P5); github.js `--add-assignee` and delegate-helper write `assignee=@github-copilot` (P6).

## Desired change

- Add `--if-assignee` CAS to `wl update` (atomic single-winner).
- herdr audit-tier claim becomes status-neutral (assignee CAS against `""`); dispatch rollback clears assignee guarded on `--if-assignee <agent>`; audit runner clears assignee on every terminal verdict path (success 'yes', failure restore, verdict 'no').
- Define the scheduling-hold convention: non-empty assignee = item intentionally held from auto-dispatch (assign → producer ⇒ hold). All skills clear assignee on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does; intake/delegate/triage reviewed).
- One-time legacy cleanup of assignee residue (698+ items).
- Drop `needsProducerReview` everywhere: migration, persistent-store/sync/jsonl, CLI/API (`wl reviewed`, filters, query params, cli-types), herdr (grouping, icons, pane-lifecycle, pane-close*, stalled-work, settings, fetcher, downtime-worker select*/classify), theme.ts, interview.ts, audit runner ('yes' verdict path), ship check-final-validation.js (re-homed onto assignee hold), docs.
- Sync regression guard handled per open question Q1.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — add `--if-assignee` CAS (normalizeActionArgs + update path)
- `src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `updateIfMatches`/CAS field surface, column removal, schema/CRUD
- `src/sync.ts` — merge-participating/regression-guard behaviour for `assignee` (Q1)
- `src/commands/reviewed.ts` — remove/repurpose the command
- `src/commands/list.ts`, `src/commands/search.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`, `src/commands/create.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/cli-types.ts` — remove `--needs-producer-review` options/param
- `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`, `src/theme.ts` — producer-review icon/flags
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — flag explain/clear flow (replace or update)
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — drop-column migration
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — status-neutral `claimWorkItem` + guarded `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (+ `--if-assignee`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch claim/rollback/select*/classifyItemForDispatch (filtering moves to assignee-based)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, pane-lifecycle/stalled-work/settings — `needsProducerReview` icon/logic removal
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents) — clear assignee on terminal verdicts; 'yes' verdict producer-hold
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents) — assignee-clear conventions (already on failure)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` (SorraAgents) — release gate re-homed onto assignee hold (+ `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`)
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`, `tests/cli/*`, `tests/unit/*`, migration tests
- Docs: `AGENTS.md` (both repos), `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/icons-design.md`

## Related work

- WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL — root cause bug (depends-on blocker of this epic; its intake interview on fix approach + repo boundary is awaiting producer answers)
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (CAS claim design point 1; RC-1 single-claim guarantee this epic must preserve)
- WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH — downtime dispatcher hard-strikes on retired 'in_progress' stage (retired-stage `migrateStage` claim path in fetcher.ts)
- WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A — cross-root coordination offers (per-call `--worklog-dir` claim targeting; P3 cross-root concern)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — herdr: flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale
- WL-0MU72WJ8C0005GIE — herdr dispatcher ignores needsProducerReview on live dispatch path
- WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F — downtime dispatcher excludes items needing producer review from selection
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first (dispatch ordering)
- WL-0MT32F908002YFFA — recover items stranded by marker-write-failed / spawn-failed
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr audit tier re-checks for fresh audit after selection
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion
- SA side (SorraAgents): audit runner items, ship gate items (linked during planning)

## Out of scope

- Option B (audit_runner `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` addition) — keep as fallback if Option A is blocked; the bug's intake recommends a staged interim audit-runner fix (Option B as a small SA-side item first), which is tracked on the root-cause bug, not here.
- Changing the implement/plan/intake tiers' status flip (they are legitimately in_progress while worked).

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Assignee-hold convention breaks existing flows.** Any skill that leaves a non-empty assignee (intake, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`) silently suppresses future auto-dispatch. Mitigation: audit every assignee writer, clear on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does), document in AGENTS.md, and add a test that a cleared claim re-enables dispatch.
- **R2 — Legacy residue cleanup could strand live items.** The one-time cleanup of 698 completed + 7 in_review assigned items must run after the code change ships, be idempotent, and scope to audit-hold residue only (not e.g. in-flight implement claims).
- **R3 — Release-gate weakening.** Re-homing the ship gate onto the assignee hold must not make unreviewed items shippable. Mitigation: gate checks producer-assigned items for a passing audit ('Ready to close: Yes') before closeWorkItemsAfterRelease.
- **R4 — Cross-repo coordination.** Skill-side changes (audit_runner, status_lifecycle, ship gate) live in SorraAgents; if they are not tracked/implemented via SA work items, the epic's AC "no references left" cannot be met. Assumed: SA items are created during planning (pending the bug's repo-boundary answer).
- **R5 — Sync regression guard fights assignee clearing** (P3) and **R6 — `--if-assignee` needs full CAS semantics** (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, mirrors `--if-status`/`--if-stage`; introduced in `wl update` only, not other commands) — both captured in ACs (9 and 1).

## Open questions (Appendix)

- Q1 (sync regression guard, P3): (a) treat `assignee` as a normal non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate cross-root, or (b) accept `assignee` as an owned reconciliation field and document the cross-root rule? **Recommended: (a)** — the status-neutral claim's whole point is that the cleared assignee must propagate so the item is re-selectable everywhere; a regression-guarded assignee resurrects claims across panes/roots and would need `--accept-regressions` noise on every sync. **OPEN QUESTION — deferred to implementation; both keep the epic ACs intact.**
- Q2 (producer-hold assignee value, P5/P7): what literal value marks the producer hold (e.g. operator identity `rog`, a reserved `producer` sentinel, or `@github-copilot`-style)? **Recommended: a reserved well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity used by the release gate** so the hold is self-describing; exact value to be confirmed with the producer. **OPEN QUESTION — record the operator's identity during planning.**
- Q3 (dependency direction): this epic currently holds `depends-on` → WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL (the root-cause bug it resolves), leaving it `blocked`. Confirm this is intentional sequencing (bug root-cause decided first) vs. the epic superseding the bug. **Recommended: keep depends-on on the root cause until its intake decision lands, then have the epic's completion close the bug as fixed-by (recorded as related work; direction reviewed at planning).** **OPEN QUESTION — traceability reviewed during planning.**

*Source: repository inspection (fetcher.ts, downtime-worker.ts, sync.ts, reviewed.ts, interview.ts, migrations, SorraAgents skill tree), bug intake records, and work-item history. No interactive interview conducted — herdr-dispatched session; seed context was exhaustive.*

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN1B8MKZS** – Implement next command (completed)
- **WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI** – Change in_review icons and reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msrbffln005w3vt, 0mtq14w7l003ii5a, accept, acceptance, add (+300 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mtq14w7l003ii5a, accept, add, addition, agent (+270 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, add, added, addition, agent (+232 more)

# Intake Brief: CTRL-r manual refresh shortcut + remove `[auto-refresh on]` header indicator

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list can only refresh via the event-driven watcher / 30 s auto-refresh tick; there is no reliable manual-refresh key. The legacy `r` refresh was removed (commit `6b98e67b`, WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA) because `r` is now a chord leader (Producer Review / Interview), leaving the `refresh` action in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` unreachable from list mode. Separately, the header always shows a `[auto-refresh on]` message while `autoRefresh` is enabled — visual noise that the user wants gone.

## Users

- **Operator / TUI user of the herdr worklist selection list** — wants an immediate, unambiguous "refresh now" key so edited items appear without waiting for the auto-refresh cycle, and wants a cleaner header.

User stories:
- As a worklist user, when I press `Ctrl+r`, the selection list immediately re-fetches items from the worklog DB and re-renders, preserving my selection when the item still exists.
- As a worklist user, I want the header to stop showing `[auto-refresh on]` so the header stays short and conveys only count/filter/status.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing `Ctrl+r` (`\x12`) while the worklist is in **list mode** immediately triggers the existing refresh path (`doRefresh(true)`): items are re-fetched from the DB, the list re-renders, and the currently selected item stays selected when it still exists in the refreshed list. Covered by a `handleKeypress` unit test (`keyToAction('\x12') === 'refresh'`).
2. `Ctrl+r` does **not** conflict with the `r` chord leader: bare `r` continues to start the Producer Review / Interview chords (`r p`, `r i`) exactly as today, and no chord/shortcut changes are made to `shortcuts.json`.
3. The `[auto-refresh on]` segment is **never rendered** in the header, regardless of the `autoRefresh` setting. Header rendering keeps the count / filter / `(top N of M)` / `[paused — hidden]` / downtime segments. The renderer test that currently asserts `[auto-refresh on]` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` ~L5915) is updated to assert its absence, and header-fit tests still pass.
4. `Ctrl+r` remains functional when `autoRefresh` is disabled (the setting still controls the scheduler tick; the shortcut is independent of it).
5. Manual refresh is documented: `packages/herdr/README.md` gains a `Ctrl+r` entry in the navigation/keybindings section, and any stale references to "manual `r`" refresh (README ~L266 "Manual `r` always runs", `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` ~L38) are updated to `Ctrl+r`.
6. **Testing/validation criterion:** full `packages/herdr` unit suite (`worklist*.test.ts`) passes with the changes.
7. **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (README keybindings + stale `r` refresh references; the worklist renderer comment noting the parameter's retained-for-compatibility status).
8. **Suite criterion:** full project test suite (`npm test` → vitest) passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The legacy `r` refresh must NOT be restored (it conflicts with the `r` chord leader — WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA); `Ctrl+r` is the new binding.
- Do not change `shortcuts.json`; the `r` chords, `S` Ship It, and all other bindings stay as-is.
- No change to the auto-refresh *schedule* or DB-change gating — only the header message is removed and a manual refresh shortcut is added.
- The `refresh` action already exists end-to-end (`keyToAction` → `handleKeypress` `case 'refresh'` → `handleKeyInput` `if (action === 'refresh') → doRefresh(true)`); the change just re-instates a reachable key for it.
- Keyboard scope: list mode only (the user asked for the *selection list*; the detail view keeps its current behaviour). KeypressDecoder already emits a lone control char (`\x12`) as its own token, so no decoder change is needed.
- Live keyboard blink: `\x12` is not a herdr prefix/leader and is not bound elsewhere; no conflicts known.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `keyToAction()` (L~2852) maps navigation keys; the `r → refresh` case was removed by commit `6b98e67b` (WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA). The `case 'refresh'` in `handleKeypress` (L~3073) and `if (action === 'refresh') { await doRefresh(true); }` (L~6385) are still present but unreachable in list mode.
  - Renderer `createListRenderer` (L~3835) header block (L~3966-3968): `if (autoRefresh) { header += ' ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}'; }`. `autoRefresh` is passed positionally from the single production call site (`opts.autoRefresh`, L~6618) and by many tests.
  - `doRefresh(true)` (L~5511) already preserves selection across refreshes (item matched by ID).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — L~5915 asserts header contains `[auto-refresh on]`; several header-fit tests pass `autoRefresh` positionally.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — `r`-chord-leader tests at ~L542-554.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — §2 navigation list (no refresh entry); L~266 "Manual `r` always runs"; L~1422/1592 "manual actions never gated".
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` L~38 — "`r`/`S`-style refreshes".

## Desired change

1. **Bind `Ctrl+r`.** In `keyToAction()` add `case '\x12': return 'refresh';` (Ctrl+R is byte 0x12). Because `\x12` is not a chord leader and not a single-key shortcut, the existing `action === 'refresh'` branch fires `doRefresh(true)` — the immediate, selection-preserving refresh. No changes to `shortcuts.json`, the chord registry, or the decoder.
2. **Remove the header indicator.** Delete the `if (autoRefresh) { header += ' [auto-refresh on]'; }` block in the renderer. Keep the `autoRefresh` parameter (positional callers across the codebase/tests depend on it) but mark it intentionally unused with a comment, OR cleanly remove it if the implementer verifies no positional caller shifts break. Recommended: keep the parameter with a documented "retained for positional call-site compatibility" comment (surgical, no test churn beyond the indicator assertions).
3. Update the header tests to assert the indicator is absent, add a `keyToAction('\x12')`/`handleKeypress` Ctrl+r test, and add a README keybinding entry + fix stale `r` references.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `keyToAction` (\x12 → 'refresh'), renderer header block removal, parameter compatibility comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — header-indicator test update (L~5915), new Ctrl+r mapping test, header-fit test hygiene.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — verify/add Ctrl+r coverage alongside the `r`-chord-leader tests (L~542).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — §2 keybinding list + L~266 manual-refresh wording.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — L~38 "`r`/`S`-style refreshes" → `Ctrl+r`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "selection list view" = the Herdr worklist pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) — its header is the only place `[auto-refresh on]` renders. The Pi TUI browse widget has no such header and is out of scope (confirmed by searching both `packages/herdr` and `packages/tui`).
- **Assumption (based on the explicit "use CTRL-r" directive):** the binding is `Ctrl+r` (byte `\x12`) and replaces any notion of bare-`r` refresh, which remains reserved for the review/interview chords.
- **Risk — dead parameter:** left unused, `autoRefresh` in the renderer becomes dead weight; mitigation = documented compatibility comment (or clean removal if the implementer verifies positional callers).
- **Risk — stale docs:** README `Manual `r`` claims (L~266, L~1422/1592) and `pause-when-hidden.md` already reference a removed `r` refresh; update them with the CTRL-r wording so documentation doesn't point at a non-existent key.
- **Scope-creep risk:** removing the `[paused — hidden]` indicator, changing the auto-refresh interval, or re-adding bare-`r` refresh are all out of scope; anything discovered during implementation should be recorded as a linked work item, not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA** (completed) — removed the legacy `r → refresh` mapping ("fix(herdr): remove legacy r->refresh mapping in list mode", commit `6b98e67b`); rationale this change must not reverse.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** (completed) — shortcut commands (close/delete/update) now refresh the selection list immediately; same `doRefresh` path.
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** (completed) — 5 s auto-refresh for the *Pi TUI* browse selection list (different widget, useful context).
- **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** (completed) — staleness indicator in the selection list when its refresh is paused (related header/footer rendering area).
- **WL-0MS31X52O0061C79** (completed) — auto-refresh & auto-sync implementation that introduced the `[auto-refresh on]` header segment (`ac76444a`).
- **WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ** (completed) — DB-change gated auto-refresh with "Manual `r` always runs" wording.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should `Ctrl+r` also refresh while in the detail view, or just the selection list?" — Not asked: the seed explicitly scopes to the **selection list view**; list-mode-only is the reasonable default and is recorded as an assumption (AC 1). If the producer wants detail-view refresh too, AC 1 can be widened.
- Q2: "Should the auto-refresh *schedule* change (interval/DB-gate) or only the header message?" — Not asked: the seed says "Remove the message", not the feature; the setting remains functional (AC 4).
- Q3: No clarifying questions required — seed context was unambiguous and all other details were resolved by repo research (header location, existing refresh action, chord conflict, docs references). Any deviation the producer wants (e.g. detail-mode scope) is a small AC amendment.

## Effort and risk (preliminary)

- **Effort:** Small (XS–S) — a one-line key mapping, a 3-line header deletion, test updates and doc wording. No new modules or settings.
- **Risk:** Low — touches a well-covered unit surface (`keyToAction`, header renderer); no lifecycle/status/DB semantics; the main care points are not resurrecting bare-`r` and keeping positional renderer callers intact.

## RM summary (research)

Confirmed the legacy `r → refresh` mapping was removed in commit `6b98e67b` (WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA) leaving the `refresh` action dead in list mode; confirmed the `[auto-refresh on]` header segment is unique to the Herdr worklist renderer (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` L~3967, introduced by `ac76444a`/WL-0MS31X52O0061C79) and appears in only one test assertion (L~5915); confirmed `KeypressDecoder`/`splitKeypresses` passes lone control characters through unchanged so `\x12` arrives as a single token; confirmed `\x12` is not a chord leader and no shortcut binds it, so the existing `action === 'refresh' → doRefresh(true)` handler is reachable with no registry changes; surveyed docs for stale `r` refresh references (README L~266, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` L~38). No completed or open item duplicates this work (existing items cover Pi-TUI browse auto-refresh and post-command refresh, not a Ctrl+r binding or header cleanup).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP** – Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer (completed)
- **WL-0MQK8EBNT002XMR7** – wl list --parent <id> does not include childCount in JSON output (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG5ZD1DHKPCV** – Feature: Automation ergonomics (sort/limit/fields/bulk) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, auto, ctrl, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, keyboard, list, manual, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, auto, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, keyboard, list, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, auto, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, list, manual, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist

# Test-first: assignee-CAS claim and status-neutral audit-dispatch contract

Author the failing tests that pin the contract for child C2 (`wl update --if-assignee`) and child C4 (status-neutral audit-tier claim). This item is deliberately created **before** the implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Goal (user story)

As an agent, I want executable tests that define the exact assignee-CAS and status-neutral claim behaviour, so the implementation is driven by a failing-first contract and regressions in the claim path are caught immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Regression test: herdr dispatch claim → simulated audit Phase-2 failure → item back at completed/in_review, re-selectable (no in-progress/plan_complete, no needsProducerReview-column dependency).
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] Unit tests exist for `wl update --if-assignee <value>`: exact-match success, mismatch is a no-op/stale result with no partial write, `--if-assignee ""` succeeds when the current assignee is empty, and `--if-assignee ""` fails when the assignee is non-empty.
- [ ] Atomicity test: two concurrent `--if-assignee ""` claims against the same item yield exactly one winner (single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction).
- [ ] Integration test: a `completed`/`in_review` item claimed by the audit tier reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` — never an `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid.

Failing-first test files plus a comment recording the red/green evidence.

# Add `wl update --if-assignee` atomic CAS

## Goal (user story)

As an agent competing for a work item, I want an atomic assignee compare-and-swap guard on `wl update`, so a status-neutral claim can have exactly one winner without changing the item's status or stage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl update` supports `--if-assignee` CAS (atomic, single-winner; unit + integration tests).
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] `wl update <id> --assignee <v> --if-assignee <expected>` applies only when the current assignee matches `expected`; on mismatch it returns a stale/no-op result and writes nothing.
- [ ] The guard runs in a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction through the `updateIfMatches` CAS primitive (the expected-match surface is extended to `assignee`).
- [ ] `--if-assignee ""` is a meaningful expected value (matches an empty assignee) and is distinguishable from the flag being omitted.
- [ ] `--if-assignee` composes with `--if-status`/`--if-stage` in one atomic guard; existing `--if-status`/`--if-stage` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] The C1 unit + CLI integration tests pass; `CLI.md` documents the new flag.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `updateIfMatches`/`UpdateWorkItemInput` expected-match typing to include `assignee` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`, `src/persistent-store.ts`, `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`).
- Add `--if-assignee <assignee>` to the update command and wire it into the existing CAS branch (`src/commands/update.ts`: option, `normalizeActionArgs`, `hasProvided` normalisation, `updateIfMatches` call, stale-result message).
- Normalise the empty string as an explicit expected value (mirroring the assignee normalisation used for writes).

## Constraints

- Atomicity and single-winner semantics must match the existing `--if-status`/`--if-stage` claim (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1).
- Do not change other commands' CAS surface.

**Key Files:**

- `src/commands/update.ts`
- `src/persistent-store.ts`, `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
- `./CLI.md`, `tests/cli/*`

CLI flag, store CAS support, tests, `CLI.md` entry.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator syncing across roots, I want a decided, documented and tested rule for how `assignee` merges, so a cleared assignee (releasing a scheduling hold) propagates cross-root instead of being refused as a regression and resurrecting stale claims.

# Status-neutral audit-tier claim and guarded rollback (herdr)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator running herdr downtime dispatch, I want the audit-tier claim to change only the assignee, so an audited `completed`/`in_review` item never enters a hybrid state and a failed audit can never strand it off the review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) issues `wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""` — it writes no `--status` and no `--stage`.
- [ ] The item reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` throughout the claim (no `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid).
- [ ] `rollbackClaimWorkItem` clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`, so only this claim's state is reverted.
- [ ] Exactly-one-winner is preserved (the C1 concurrency test passes).
- [ ] `classifyItemForDispatch`/the audit-tier `select*` functions exclude items with a non-empty assignee, so assigning an item to the producer makes the claim fail stale at every tier.
- [ ] Tests cover: claim keeps completed/in_review; concurrent claim single-winner; an assignee-held item is not dispatched.

## Constraints

- **No hybrid status/stage write**: the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`.
- The `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback is guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`.
- Cross-root claim targeting keeps the existing `--worklog-dir` convention.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`claimWorkItem`, `rollbackClaimWorkItem`)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`

Status-neutral claim, guarded rollback, assignee-based selection exclusion, tests.

# Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, I want an explicit per-item way to pause automatic scheduling — by assigning the item to myself — that does not rely on a magic DB flag, with a well-known sentinel value the release gate can recognise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] Epic open question Q2 is answered and recorded: the literal producer-hold value is a reserved, well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity (self-describing, reusable by the release gate). **Recommended:** reserved identity value, exact literal confirmed with the producer.
- [ ] The convention is documented: a non-empty assignee means "intentionally held from auto-dispatch"; assigning to the producer is the per-item pause switch.

# Show what an item is blocked on (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8)

## Problem statement

When browsing work items in the Herdr selection list, the metadata panel shows status, stage, priority and other fields but not *what* a blocked item is waiting on. A user who sees a blocked item must leave the list (or run `wl dep list <id>` by hand) to discover the blocking work items, so the "blocked" signal is not actionable at a glance.

## Users

- **Producers / triage engineers** browsing the Herdr worklist who need to understand why an item cannot proceed.
- **Dispatch operators** who inspect a blocked candidate before deciding whether to escalate its blocker.
- **Developers** who want to see which dependency edge is holding an item up without leaving the pane.

### Example user stories

- As a **producer**, I want to see the ID and title of every work item blocking the selected item, so that I can decide whether to unblock it or prioritise the blocker.
- As a **dispatch operator**, I want the blocked-by information in the selection list metadata panel (not only the detail view), so that I can triage without switching views.
- As a **developer**, I want the blockers shown even when the item's stored `status` is still `open` (dependency-blocked), so that I am not misled by a stale status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When the selected item has at least one **active blocker** (an outbound `depends-on` edge whose target is neither `completed`/`deleted` nor at stage `in_review`/`done`), the Herdr selection-list metadata panel renders a `Blocked By` entry at the **end of the metadata section** (after the existing metadata rows, before the description preview).
- [ ] Each active blocker is rendered as its own `Blocked By` row in the form `Blocked By  WL-xxxxxxxx — <title>`, one row per blocker, so both the ID and title are visible.
- [ ] The `Blocked By` row(s) appear for **any** selected item with active blockers, regardless of the item's stored `status` (so dependency-blocked `open` items are covered), and are omitted entirely when there are no active blockers.
- [ ] Completed/terminal dependencies (`completed`, `deleted`, `in_review`, `done`) are **not** listed as blockers.
- [ ] Blocker resolution failure is fail-open: a failed/unparseable `wl dep list` lookup yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation (consistent with `resolveMetaLastCommand`).
- [ ] The metadata panel continues to scroll correctly (`m`/`M`) with the extra rows, and the panel never overflows its allocated rows.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: rendering one row per active blocker with ID + title; omission when no active blockers; filtering of terminal blockers; the dependency-blocked-but-`open` case; and the fail-open path.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the Herdr selection-list metadata panel only.** The detail view and the Pi TUI are out of scope; the change must not alter their rendering.
- **No new dependency edges are created or mutated** — this is a read-only display change.
- **Reuse existing semantics and helpers** where possible: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) for the "still blocks" predicate, and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) for parsing `wl dep list <id> --json`.
- **Fail-open**: dependency look-up errors must degrade to "no blocked-by rows", never to a thrown error in the render path.
- **No list-data shape regression**: `WorkItem` consumers (list rows, filters, dispatch) must be unaffected by any added optional field.
- **Consistent with the metadata-panel conventions** established by `buildMetaRows`/`pairMetaRows` and the icon/label formatting (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9).

## Existing state

- The selection-list metadata panel is rendered by `formatMetadataPanel()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, which builds rows via `buildMetaRows()` (paired with `pairMetaRows()`), then appends a markdown-rendered description preview. Rows are label/value pairs; the panel scrolls independently via `metaScrollOffset`.
- `formatMetadataPanel()` is called from `createListRenderer()` with the selected row, and the renderer already receives a per-selection enrichment value (`metaLastCommand`, resolved by `resolveMetaLastCommand()` in the main loop). That parameter is the established precedent for selection-scoped data.
- `WorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) currently carries no dependency/blocker data; no `wl dep list` call is made for list items. `wl next`/`wl list`/`wl show` JSON does not include blocker edges.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` returns `outbound` edges with `id`, `title`, `status`, `priority` and `direction: depends-on`. `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` already parses this; `isActiveBlocker()` already defines the active-blocker predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` already resolves critical blockers via `wl dep list` for the downtime dispatcher (`fetchCriticalBlockers`), so the command/JSON shape is proven.
- The completed TUI work items WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU / WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1 established the "Blocking"/"Blocked by" rendering precedent in the TUI details pane; the Herdr selection list currently has no equivalent.

## Desired change

When the selection-list metadata panel renders the selected item, resolve that item's outbound `depends-on` edges, keep only the **active** blockers, and append one `Blocked By` row per blocker at the end of the metadata section:

```
Blocked By  WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W — worklist.ts: pre-dialog gate + freeze-on-confirm integration
```

- Lookup is performed for the **selected** item only (not every list row), on selection change, with best-effort caching keyed by item ID and refreshed with the list refresh; the render path must not block on it.
- The panel already scrolls, so no `+N more` truncation is required (decision Q3-A).
- No blockers → no `Blocked By` rows; the panel is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — add a `blockedBy` parameter to `formatMetadataPanel()` and `createListRenderer()`; render one `Blocked By` row per blocker at the end of the metadata rows; keep panel truncation/scroll behaviour intact.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — add an optional `blockedBy?: Array<{ id: string; title: string }>` field to `WorkItem` (or a dedicated resolver result type) and a `fetchBlockersForItem(id)` helper running `wl dep list <id> --json`, filtering via the active-blocker predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — reuse the exported `isActiveBlocker()` predicate (no change expected; import if needed).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reuse the exported `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` parser (no change expected; import if needed).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (main TUI loop) — resolve blockers for the selected item alongside `resolveMetaLastCommand()` and pass them into the renderer; fail-open on lookup error.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for `formatMetadataPanel` blocked-by rendering, filtering, omission and scrolling.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` — tests for the new blocker fetch/parse helper (active filtering, terminal filtering, failure path).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new `Blocked By` metadata rows.

## Related work

- **Herdr selection list should show dependency-blocked items (WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2)** — completed; added `--include-blocked` so dependency-blocked items appear in the list. This item makes their blockers visible.
- **Default Herdr list still hides blocked items despite --include-blocked (WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE)** — completed; mandatory blocked subset. Related because both concern blocked-item visibility.
- **Herdr in_review filter hides blocked items that the release gate treats as release-blocking (WL-0MV70XY6D008013C)** — completed; blocked-item filter semantics.
- **Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI (WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU)** and **TUI: Render dependency links in Details pane (WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1)** — completed; established the "Blocking"/"Blocked by" rendering precedent (TUI details pane). This item ports the *blocked-by* half into the Herdr list metadata panel.
- **Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9)** — completed; metadata-row formatting conventions this change follows.
- **Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)** and **Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)** — completed; the panel layout/scroll contract the new rows must respect.
- **Synthetic dispatch rows for the worklist (WL-0MUL2IY8L009S3PQ)** — completed; log-derived rows. Blockers are only meaningful for live rows; the implementation should skip the lookup for `isLogOnly`/`isLogDerived` rows.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** blocker resolution could grow into a general dependency browser (inbound "Blocking" rows, click-to-open, `+N more`). That is explicitly out of scope (decision Q1/Q3); any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked follow-up work item, not absorbed here.
- **Performance risk:** a `wl dep list` process spawn on every selection change could make fast arrow-key navigation feel laggy. Mitigation: resolve only the selected item, cache by ID, refresh with the list refresh, and keep the render path non-blocking (render the last-known/empty result until the lookup completes).
- **Fail-open risk:** a hung `wl dep list` could delay the lookup. Mitigation: apply the existing `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`/transient-retry pattern and treat timeout as "no blockers shown".
- **Assumption (Q1-A):** "blocked" means *has at least one active outbound dependency edge*, not merely `status=blocked`; this is required to cover dependency-blocked `open` items.
- **Assumption (Q2-A):** terminal targets (`completed`/`deleted`/`in_review`/`done`) are not shown as blockers, reusing `isActiveBlocker()`.
- **Assumption (Q3-A):** one row per blocker; the panel's existing scroll makes truncation unnecessary.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list` edges carry a usable `title`; when a title is empty the row falls back to the ID alone rather than rendering a dangling separator.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Which items should show a `Blocked By` row? (a) Any item with active (non-terminal) outbound dependency edges, regardless of stored `status`; (b) only items whose stored `status` is `blocked`; (c) both, but only dependency-blocked items that are also `status=blocked`." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: dependency-blocked items can still carry `status=open` (see `wl next --include-blocked`), and (a) is the only option that answers the question for those.
- Q2: "Which blockers should be listed? (a) Only active blockers (outbound deps not `completed`/`deleted` and not at `in_review`/`done`), matching `isActiveBlocker()`; (b) all outbound dependencies, including completed ones." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: consistent with the existing "still blocks" predicate; avoids noise from already-done blockers.
- Q3: "How should multiple blockers render in the metadata section? (a) One `Blocked By` row per blocker, each `WL-xxxx — <title>`; (b) a single `Blocked By` row listing all blockers comma-separated; (c) one row per blocker truncated after N with `+N more`." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: matches the established TUI details-pane precedent and keeps each blocker's ID + title readable; the panel already scrolls, so no truncation is needed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MM04HDI618Y7DT0** – Add dependency-blocker filter tests (completed)
- **WL-0MUDELHIH009O0AX** – TUI integration tests for ship guard (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, block, blocked, data, end, herdr, line, list, meta, one, provide, section, selection, show, title
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, block, blocked, data, end, herdr, line, list, meta, one, provide, section, selection, show, title
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, block, blocked, data, end, herdr, line, list, meta, one, provide, section, selection, show, title

## Re-implemented per written ACs (findings F1/F2/F3 closed)

Resolved the three producer questions from the re-open against the **written AC text** (the contract), and closed F1/F2/F3. Committed to dev as 16062fc4.

### F1 (AC2) — running-pane check now implemented
A tab only blocks demotion when it is a **running pane**: its `agent_status` is not `done`/`exited` (mirrors `countRunningDowntimePanes` / `pane-close-herdr` terminal semantics). The production tab list now threads `agent_status` through `parseTabListOutput` → `HydratorTab.agent_status` (new optional field). Absent/unknown status fails open toward active (never demote on untrustworthy evidence, AC5). `runHydrationOnce` uses the new liveness-aware `isActivePaneMatch`. A pane left by a finished agent no longer keeps its claim stuck in in_progress — the exact stale-claim case the feature exists to fix. The selection-list marker (WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ) intentionally retains tab-existence semantics via `collectTabWorkItemIds`.

### F2 (AC5) — production log sink wired
`createProductionHydratorDeps()` now returns a real `log`: a bounded, fail-open file sink (`createHydratorFileLog` → `<worklog root>/.worklog/logs/hydrator.log`, rolling 200 lines, atomic temp+rename). A failing cycle is operator-observable instead of silently retrying every 30 s.

### F3 (AC3) — else-branch stage follows written AC
`decideDemotion` else-branch now returns `{status: open, stage: intake_complete}` exactly as AC3 states (was preserving the claimed stage). Documented decision: the re-open asked whether to keep the claimed stage; no producer answer arrived and the AC text is explicit, so the written AC governs. Producer can veto at review.

### AC3 stage-aware blockers (stated Minimal Implementation)
`wl dep list` carries status only; the item's Minimal Implementation requires fetching stage via `wl show` for non-completed/deleted edges so the blocked-vs-open decision matches `isDependencyActive` (target at `in_review`/`done` is not a blocker). Production `listOutboundDeps` now enriches edges with their stage, failing open when `wl show` is unavailable.

data.comment:
Producer-rejection fix (input responsiveness): RCA complete.

ROOT CAUSE: watchDbChanges watched the SQLite worklog.db / -wal / -shm files in addition to the state counter. The pane's own refresh path (fetchActionableCount + fetchChildrenForItems, from WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) opens a FRESH WorklogDatabase connection per read, and that open/close checkpoints the WAL (~24 MB observed) and touches -shm — i.e. it modifies exactly the watched files. Each refresh therefore re-fired the watch → another refresh → a SELF-SUSTAINING refresh storm that saturated the event loop and made keyboard input (e.g. a-a) unresponsive. Verified empirically: opening a WorklogDatabase on the live DB checkpointed and removed the 24 MB -wal/-shm; opening bare-DB copies bumped the db mtime.

FIX (surgical, plugin-local): watch ONLY the state-counter file (the write-only signal  bumps on every write via preAction invalidation and after sync). The pane never writes the counter, so the loop is broken at its source; every real agent write still fires the watch within 150 ms debounce. The 30 s tick remains the fail-open fallback; idle zero-spawn preserved. requestWatchRefresh also re-checks the counter after the refresh (the counter is bumped before the write commits) so the pane never shows a pre-commit snapshot.

TESTS: rewrote db-change.test.ts to the counter-only contract; added real-fs.watch regression (SQLite -wal/-shm/db churn alone never fires) + end-to-end worklist-watch.test.ts regression (DB-file churn does not wake the pane; the counter still does). Both fail against the old code (proved). 43/43 herdr watch tests + 103 herdr test files green; full build green.

Recorded follow-up: WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B (single shared in-process connection per refresh) for the residual per-refresh sync DB-open cost.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Rework (producer rejection: marker does not update to current status/open panes).

Root cause: the display marker was only applied inside `doRefresh`, which the periodic refresh/sync ticks gate on a worklog DB change. Opening or closing a work-item tab does NOT touch the worklog DB, so the marker could not appear/clear for it until an unrelated DB write happened (the focus-resume fallback was also DB-gated).

Fix:
- `hydrator.ts`: `markItemsActiveByTab` is now idempotent — it captures each item's pre-marker worklog status in a non-enumerable `Symbol` and restores it on every pass, so a closed tab clears the marker (and a re-opened tab restores it) without a `wl` re-fetch.
- `worklist.ts`: new `active-tab-marker` scheduler task on the hydrator cadence (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) plus a focus-resume re-apply, both independent of the DB-change gate. The task spawns only `herdr tab list` (never `wl`), preserving the zero-`wl`-when-idle guarantee, and is visibility/typing gated. Added `WorkItemListState.allItems()` so the marker covers the unfiltered set.
- Tests: idempotency + serialization-shape unit tests (`hydrator.test.ts`); a worklist integration test that closes a tab with the refresh tick disabled for longer than the marker cadence and asserts the marker clears (would fail without the new task).
- Docs: hydrator module header, `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`.

Full suite green (scope=full). Commit fc23a8ed pushed to dev.
